News.title: England return to proper Test cricket with gritty batting performance
News.content:
Cox unfurled some fine drives and assessed conditions like a veteran, scoring quickly to a run-a-ball 38 but only six more from his next 48 as Pakistan knocked over partners at the other end. It was vital Cox stayed in to stabilise the innings. It is the job of a No 3 to attack or defend; calibrate their game to what is required at the time. Cox, when he played briefly for England in New Zealand two winters ago and before injury cut short his tour, looked to be a player drunk on the Bazball fumes. He was out in a warm-up match against a New Zealand XI in Queenstown hooking and flailing at the ball. This was his second mature performance in a row, an innings of 55 to follow his 73 at Leeds and this was made in much harder circumstances.

Pakistan were better after their Headingley horror show. Mohammad Abbas must feel more at home on a dank London day than he does in Sialkot, and can earn a place on the honours board if he nicks the last England wicket after taking four for 56. Mohammad Ali bowled some jaffas, and some rubbish, for three for 67 and spinner Usman Ali kept it tight and found some turn before losing control as Smith went after him. England still scored at 4.4 an over a reflection of some of the wasted deliveries by Pakistan and 10 no-balls.

Inevitably they were a mixed bag in the field. Three dropped catches were redeemed by a run out and a world-class grab at slip by Salman Ali Agha – captain last week, left out here – to dismiss Cox when he lost his shape trying to hit the ball too hard.

News.title: Ebola response shifts to Congo’s river network
News.content:
Stacked with logs and crammed with hundreds of passengers, the giant barges are nudged day after day along one of Africa’s greatest waterways.

The weeks-long voyage looks sedate, but the tugs are pushing their heavily-laden charges along an unstoppable aquatic superhighway.

Sharing the Congo river with these trade behemoths are canoes, fishing boats and smaller wooden cargo ships.

The river connects the wild east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to the capital Kinshasa, in a vital economic artery and transport corridor nearly 1,100 miles long.

The waterway is a lifeline for passengers, timber, produce and goods. Roads are rare and unreliable, and airfares are far too expensive for most.

Now there are concerns the river risks becoming a conduit for something else heading to the capital of nearly 18 million people: the deadly Ebola virus.

News.title: Great British fry-up implicated in Salmonella outbreak
News.content:
The outbreak, which involved packets of chicken-flavoured instant dried noodles, was traced back to a manufacturing plant near Kyiv, according to an assessment issued by the European Centre for Disease Control (ECDC) in June.

“Epidemiological investigations have found that cases in Denmark, Estonia, Germany, Latvia and Lithuania had consumed flavoured noodle products from the same brand. Investigations have linked the products, which were distributed in several countries, to the same producer in Ukraine,” the ECDC said in a statement at the time.

Another outbreak, which lasted from 2021 to 2024, sickened 174 people in the UK and killed one. It was linked to frozen, steam-cooked chicken breast fillets produced in Ukraine.

Although it is not known if the latest outbreak is linked to Ukraine (the UK also imports eggs from countries including Poland, Spain, and Belgium ), Ukraine sits outside of the EU and Salmonella contamination is common in many of the country’s poultry farms.

A senior figure investigating a connected outbreak of Salmonella in the Netherlands told The Telegraph that the “working hypothesis” among British health officials is that the contaminated products have come from Ukraine.

“In Ukraine, thousands of salmonellosis cases are reported each year. The highest incidence is observed among children,” said a study published in the academic journal Advances in Animal and Veterinary Sciences earlier this year.

“The main sources of the pathogen are eggs, chicken meat, and meat and dairy products. Analysis shows that frequent outbreaks are associated with poor food storage conditions [...] predominantly in the southeastern regions of Ukraine,” added the authors from the Institute of Laboratory Diagnostics and Veterinary-Sanitary Expertise in Kyiv.

Britain’s egg consumption has boomed over the last two decades, with 209 eaten per person on average every year compared to roughly 163 per person in 2000.

The rise is thought to have been driven by a spike in baking during the pandemic, the rise of brunch culture and the rise of a focus on diets rich in protein among the young, according to experts.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola’s BARBER confirms Liverpool transfer as £120million star heads for trim before medical
Sports.content:
BRADLEY BARCOLA’S barber has confirmed his Liverpool transfer in a series of Instagram posts.

The Paris Saint-Germain winger is set to fly to Merseyside this weekend for a medical before his blockbuster £120million move to Anfield.



Andoni Iraola‘s side have been chasing the France international virtually all summer.

And ahead of next Tuesday’s transfer deadline, they appear to have got their man.



Barber Enzo Dias, whose studio is located 45 minutes east of PSG’s Parc des Princes home, has been Barcola’s hairdresser of choice for a while.

In his latest Instagram story showing off his pal’s trim, Dias wrote: “Last cut before Liverpool”.



He then posted it separately, adding: “Last ride for @bradley_dls before he leaves”.

The barber, who has also shared selfies with Keylor Navas and Willian Pacho, went on to upload a picture of a Barcola PSG shirt hanging in his studio, with the further message: “Thank you for everything my brother”.



Barcola, 23, is set to be Liverpool’s marquee summer signing.

The France international joined PSG from Lyon in 2023 and has enjoyed a glittering three-year stint at Parc des Princes.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Barcola has played 152 times for the French giants, scoring 39 goals and laying on 37 assists.

The speedy star has won several major trophies, including three Ligue 1 titles and two Champions Leagues.

He was an unused substitute for PSG’s Uefa Super Cup triumph earlier this month.



But he has since been left out by boss Luis Enrique amid intense speculation regarding his future.

Barcola’s move to Liverpool could see Tottenham land Cody Gakpo before the transfer deadline.

Gakpo is also of interest to Manchester City, although Enzo Maresca‘s side are set to prioritise Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye.

Sports.title: Chelsea hiring £19,000-a-year payroll admin to ensure mega-rich stars – on a combined £155.5m a year – get paid on time
Sports.content:
PREMIER League giants Chelsea are looking to hire a payroll administrator offering as little as £19,000 a year to make sure their mega-rich stars get paid on time.

The club has an annual first-team squad wage bill of £155.5million — one of the top flight’s highest.



But the stars’ salaries will dwarf the £19,000-£40,000 on offer, depending on experience, for the admin worker.

Chelsea’s top earner is captain Reece James on £250,000 a week, closely followed by defender Wesley Fofana who rakes in £200,000 weekly.



Wantaway Argentine ace Enzo Fernandez trousers £180,000 a week, while new £117million signing Morgan Rogers is on £150,000.

The successful applicant, based at ­Stamford Bridge stadium in West London, will be full-time.

As well as sorting out wages for the players and 1,800 permanent and casual staff at the club, they will also dish out P45s if stars go.

The job’s main responsibilities read: “Processing of end-to-end payroll for 1,800+ for all monthly UK permanent and casual payrolls.



“Ensuring a high standard of accuracy is maintained and all statutory legislation is adhered to.

“Processing of Maternity, Sickness, Shared Parental Leave, Paternity Leave and other absences in line with Company Policy and statutory regulations.

“Produce and reconcile all reports as required to enable the authorisation of Bacs files.

“Preparation of payslips & P45’s.”

Applicants don’t need any qualifications, but they do need “excellent organisational skills and attention to detail” and be good at “manual calculations.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland bursts out laughing as Man City pal Rayan Cherki swears live on TV before Sky Sports apologise
Sports.content:
RAYAN CHERKI made Erling Haaland giggle by swearing live on Sky Sports.

The Manchester City duo had just turned in an irresistible second half performance to sweep Crystal Palace aside 4-1.



Cherki, however, wasn’t so enamoured with his display in the opening 45.

Speaking moments after the match, the Frenchman told Sky: “My performance was so-so.



“In the first half, we didn’t find the space. I played so s***.

“When I see Enzo (Maresca) wants to change me, I don’t like that, and I need to show them I want to play, I want to score, I want to give an assist to Erling.

“Today I didn’t give a lot of balls to him but next time I want to give him a lot of balls.”

Haaland, who has also sworn live on Sky in the past, couldn’t help but laugh.

The Norwegian had headed City into the lead on 17 minutes.

Cherki then took over in the second period, scoring twice, including a sensational solo effort, to help his side on their way, before Haaland added another.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

On his brilliant solo effort, Cherki said: “When Erling didn’t get the ball, It’s my instinct. I’m very happy for the win today. See you next week.”

Haaland, 26, cheekily interrupted: “Just say what you actually mean. You scored two top goals!”

Man of the match Cherki added: “That is nothing. I want to give a goal for him.”

The attacking midfielder’s performance drew gushing praise from Jamie Redknapp.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Redknapp said: “Cherki painted a masterpiece with that first goal. He had an amazing effect on the game.



“He is a genius, the things that he can do with a football. He gives you that X factor.”

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres was signed to be the man to fire Arsenal to the title – now he’s looking the odd one out
Sports.content:
VIKTOR GYOKERES was signed by Arsenal to be the man who would fire them to the Premier League title.

But as the Gunners begin the defence of their crown, it is hard to escape the feeling that the Swede’s role may be changing.



Mikel Arteta’s side have started this season on fire and claimed 3-0 wins in their opening two games.

But Gyokeres played just 15 minutes in the Community Shield against Manchester City and he did not get a kick during their Prem opener against Coventry.



Kai Havertz got the nod ahead of him on both occasions and will expect to keep his place for Monday’s trip to Aston Villa.

That must be tough for Gyokeres to take as for much of last season he was the leading man, yet now it feels like the 28-year-old is part of the support cast.



It is hard to argue against Arteta backing Havertz, though, given how he has started the season.

The forward scored in the Community Shield win over City and followed that up with another goal against the Sky Blues.

There is also the fact that Arsenal’s attack just seems to flow so much better when Havertz is at the tip of it.

His link-up play brings others into the game and it is noticeable how much Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard — who also scored against Coventry — look better when 27-year-old Havertz is the team’s No 9.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But that will not make things any easier for Gyokeres to swallow.

And for all the joy that comes with the Gunners’ forward line looking so dangerous, there is an awkward question that accompanies it: What does it mean for Gyokeres?

There were hints last season that Arteta’s preferred attack would have Havertz at the heart of it.

For Arsenal’s huge trip to ­Manchester City in April, it was the German who led the line, and netted.



That was also the case for the final home game of the season against Burnley and the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain, with Havertz scoring in both of those big matches.

Mentally, that must be hard for Gyokeres to ­process.

Just over a year ago, the Swede arrived at the Emirates in a £63.5million deal as the superstar who would fire Arsenal to a first title in 22 years.

The striker took Thierry Henry’s famous No 14 shirt, not worried about the pressure that comes with it, and will argue that he delivered on his promise.

Gyokeres was Arsenal’s top scorer last season with 21 goals as they ended the season with a first title since 2004. Now, though, it is hard to shake the sense that Havertz will be the main man this term.



Or, at best for Gyokeres, that Arteta will take a ‘horses for courses approach’ and pick each striker depending on opposition.

Villa’s high and leaky defence — as shown in their opening 4-0 defeat at Brighton — could play into Gyokeres’ hands.

But even with that, it is difficult to ignore the fact that in the biggest games Arteta will likely turn to Havertz to be his No 9.

And then there is the added element of the Gunners pursuing an audacious swoop for Julian Alvarez, which is why you would love to have a penny for Gyokeres’ thoughts.

A deal for the Argentine striker looks very hard to do as Atletico Madrid do not want to sell and, if he were to leave, his preferred destination would be Barcelona.



Nonetheless, that has not stopped people talking about what he would bring to Arsenal and, in turn, overlooking what Gyokeres offers.

Speaking on Sky Sports after last week’s win over Coventry, former England defender Gary Neville said: “If Arsenal could get Alvarez somehow, that is going to light this place up.

“They’d become not just Premier League title winners, but you’re then thinking that they can go that extra step and win the Champions League as well.



“I’m being respectful to Havertz and ­Gyokeres, but if there was an Ian Wright up front for Arsenal who made those little runs all the time, Odegaard would be even ­better.”

That noise will die down when the transfer window shuts on Tuesday, and patience feels key for Gyokeres right now.

The striker is known for having a strong mentality and certainly seemed unfazed last week, chatting with his former Coventry team-mates before heading home.

Arteta also confirmed at the start of this month that the Swede will be staying, and last season showed how there are more than enough games to go around.

But playing just 15 minutes across Arsenal’s opening two matches — when they scored six goals — is always going to get people ­talking.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Gyokeres’ challenge will be, not for the first time, to prove the doubters wrong.

And, having come through plenty of tough times on his road to the top, the striker will back himself to still have a big role this season.

Sports.title: Man City ‘ready to HIJACK’ Arsenal transfer for Julian Alvarez as Atletico star skips training for third straight day
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY are reportedly thinking up a plan to commandeer Arsenal’s pursuit of Julian Alvarez.

The Atletico Madrid striker has missed training with his team-mates for three days in a row after being struck down by illness.



Marca claim that Alvarez returned to Atletico’s Cerro del Espino base on Friday afternoon to work individually with a fitness coach.

And his uncertain future has now alerted former club City, who are exploring the possibility of bringing the Argentine back to the Etihad.



Alvarez left M11 for Madrid in 2024 after growing frustrated at playing second fiddle to Erling Haaland.

He quickly established himself as one of the best strikers in Europe under Diego Simeone after finally getting the regular starting role he wanted.

But his future at Atletico has been thrown into doubt this summer, with Arsenal among a long list of clubs keeping tabs on the 26-year-old.

Barcelona have actively pursued Alvarez all summer but, after a very public spat with the their LaLiga rivals, that move is now said to be IMPOSSIBLE.

Alvarez, 26, wanted to move to the Nou Camp and has seemingly burned his bridges at Atelti.

So that leaves the Premier League as the most realistic destination if he does push for an exit.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Gunners are desperate for a top-class frontman and had been considered his most likely option in England.

But City could now enter the race.

Enzo Maresca’s side are believed to have made initial enquiries over a potential loan deal.

City’s attacking options have been weakened following the departures of Omar Marmoush and Savio.

However, there remain major hurdles to overcome before Alvarez could seal a sensational Etihad return.



The forward is reportedly reluctant to move back to England after choosing to leave City two years ago.

Atletico are also in no mood to sell cheaply and turned down a massive £130MILLION offer from city rivals Real Madrid earlier in the summer.

That means it would take a huge British record transfer fee to seal a deal.

Alternatively, the Spanish giants could demand a ready-made replacement such as Viktor Gyokeres before sanctioning his departure.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Atletico chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin reiterated on Thursday that the club want Alvarez to stay.



Simeone also made his feelings clear, saying: “I hope to help Julian continue to be as important to us as he still is.”

Sports.title: Danny Welbeck and Joao Pedro will tear it up at Chelsea — I outscored them both so I’m just waiting for my offer
Sports.content:
DANNY WELBECK, Joao Pedro and myself were all relegated with Watford in 2020.

Absolutely no one would have imagined two of those would be back together at Chelsea this season.



Having outscored the pair of them that year, I just cannot believe I didn’t get a call from someone at Stamford Bridge over the summer.

But Welbz and Joao are a fantastic duo for Chelsea to have together as the Blues look to build something different under Xabi Alonso.



Joao is primed for a big, big year. I’m not breaking any confidences when I say not making Brazil’s World Cup squad hurt him a lot.

He’s the sort of player who doesn’t just want to be in the squad, he wants to be the No 9, their main man.



That fire, a fine start against Fulham and a season without European football mean I can see him having a big year.

I don’t think he will challenge for the Golden Boot, he’s not a killer like Erling Haaland or Alexander Isak — he’s more of a rounded, complete player who likes to create as well.

But he has had that burning desire and focus to be at the top since arriving with me at Watford, when he was an 18-year-old who didn’t want to be told there was a pecking order.

And he has not changed since, I can still pick the phone up to him and have a chat whenever and he’s the same kid. Another Brazilian I played with at Watford, Richarlison, is completely the other way — I don’t recognise him now, it’s night and day.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Joao still has that fire and Welbeck is the ideal foil for him.

He used to get called Uncs, Uncle Welbeck or Welbz when we were at Watford together (above) and I’ve known him since he was at Manchester United.

He’s just infectious, a great personality, never miserable.

Trust me, Watford is a place that you can be miserable very, very quickly. I don’t think there was a day where he came in and was down.

Every time smiling, just an appreciation of playing football for a living.



He’s competitive, wants to play, wants to be fit and available — and he does the work.

Danny got off to a flying start with his header against Luton on Thursday and you could see he has already made a big impact in the dressing room by how buzzing his new team-mates were celebrating his goal.

If Alonso wants to rotate or needs to move Pedro a bit deeper, I can see Danny slotting in easily.



He can play old-school in a two, on his own, meet crosses or, as he has done at Brighton, play in a more intricate system.

He’s also in unbelievable condition. If Danny’s got his top off and you are a young lad, you’ll go, ‘Wow, who is that?’

That whole package is huge for Chelsea as they look to add some maturity to a talented squad.

And it is not just Pedro he will help. I can see him rubbing off on Cole Palmer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Being from Manchester gives them something to connect over and Palmer’s cheeky response when asked after the win over Fulham if he is ready for this new season — saying, “Did you not watch the game?” — showed me he’s been hanging around Danny.



We can’t get too overexcited by just one Prem match. But Chelsea made a good start, and if Danny can keep everyone’s heads up and Joao can maintain that form, my two Watford mates are on for a big year at the Blues.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace 1 Man City 4: Rayan Cherki’s magic inspires stunning win as Erling Haaland off the mark for the season
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA left Enzo Maresca huge shoes to fill, but also a boy with magic in his boots.

If you need someone to build a new era around, Rayan Cherki does not seem like a bad bet. Oh, and you can have Erling Haaland chipping in a few goals too.



This was not vintage Manchester City but, just like last week, they came away with three points and this time round it was more convincing.

Cherki scored twice, the first a stunning show of agility and strength, with Haaland bookending the night with a brace of his own.



Maresca wants more captains and leaders in this Manchester City squad. Haaland can do that from the front and by example, but if there is a spirit needed to define what City might become next, it could be Cherki’s – chest out and cheeky on the ball.

His first goal saw the Frenchman deal with the entire Palace back three, wriggling around Jaydee Canvot, holding off Chris Richards before lazily prodding the ball the other side of Takehiro Tomiyasu, on his knees having been so roundly tucked up.



The second, five minutes later and after Yeremy Pino’s free-kick had given the hosts hope after going in via Gianluigi Donnarumma’s back, saw him collect the ball, swivel, drive and unleash a powerful strike from range which flew past Dean Henderson with the help of a deflection.

During the scouting of Cherki, City staff noted that he compared well to Kevin de Bruyne. There is some way to go yet, but the boy is certainly heading in the right direction.

Having made a surprise appearance in midfield on the opening weekend, Marc Guehi – back at Selhurst Park for the first time since leaving in January – slotted back into defence, with Nico O’Reilly alongside Elliot Anderson in the middle.

The re-jig made sense but, early on, Maresca’s men looked unable to gain any rhythm, playing – as was his way at Chelsea – too slowly to get anything dangerous going while Palace had chances through Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada.



But it did not take long for them to go through the gears and ramp up the pressure to find the opening, with some generous defending from Palace along the way.

Antoine Semenyo was given the space to lift a looping ball into the box from the left where Haaland was able to slip through a shaky-looking back three to rise and head across goal for his first of the campaign.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Norwegian has shown he is happy to score against anyone in the Premier League since arriving.

But he has a particular fondness for Crystal Palace. Not one league game against the Eagles has gone by without Haaland finding the net, this his ninth in seven meetings.



Crystal Palace have been beset by problems this week. They were without Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr through injuries mysteriously picked up while both are seeking moves elsewhere before Tuesday’s deadline. Chadi Riad could be out for the season while Daniel Munoz was benched with his future uncertain.

So it would have been fair game, with a makeshift back line, for Palace to crumble from here.

If Phil Foden had been up to the standards we know he is capable of, then Palace probably would have done.

City’s struggling star was picked out, alone ten yards from goal, by Anderson but came closer to the Sainsbury’s roof behind The Whitehorse Lane stand than the back of the net.

He saw another close range header scrambled clear from the six-yard box moments later as Palace hung in. Foden was getting in good spots but whether it is cutting edge or confidence, something remains missing.



Pierre Sage’s side remained a threat largely due to the talent of Adam Wharton alone. Overlooked by Thomas Tuchel, who was watching from the stands, for the World Cup and a target for City themselves this summer – he was on a mission to impress. And succeeding.

Wharton’s range of passing, always fast and forwards, was on full display while he was often the one to drag the hosts up the pitch and out of danger with the ball at his feet.

It is surely too late for anyone to tempt Palace into a sale now, but it feels a dereliction of duty from the bigger clubs not to have made an attempt.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But for all his fine efforts, Cherki then shoved everyone else out of the limelight and took a firm hold on the evening.

Maresca was able to hand a debut to new man Ayyoub Bouaddi before Haaland sent a rocket into the near post to join Cherki on a brace.

Sports.title: Premier League big dogs were shamed by Super League but they’re back to self-interest and you can’t quiz their owners
Sports.content:
WHEN the Premier League was created in 1992, the principle was simple: 20 clubs, one share each, one vote each.

Thirty-four years later, the voting structure has barely changed. The balance of power certainly has.



It still operates on the principle of collective decision-making. But anyone who has sat around that table knows having an equal vote and having an equal influence are not remotely the same thing.

I spent much of my 30-plus years in football sitting at the Premier League table watching it become the world’s most commercially successful domestic competition.



I have also seen the financial gap between the biggest clubs and everyone else become enormous. That inevitably changes the politics.

The Premier League requires 14 clubs to agree to change its rules.



On paper, that protects the collective. In reality, it means six clubs can make it extremely difficult to get anything through.

That is where influence matters.

The Big Six — Manchester United, Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham — have enormous financial and political weight.

If they are united, they do not need to control the room. They just need to ensure 14 votes for change cannot be assembled.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

We have seen how powerful those relationships can become, with clubs such as Newcastle — backed by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund — finding themselves aligned with positions favoured by the bigger clubs.

Again, that is not necessarily sinister. It is football politics. Clubs vote according to what they believe is in their interests.

But it does demonstrate the difference between having one vote and having influence over others.

And there is an interesting history here.

The Big Six were once a much closer political bloc. Then came the European Super League, a spectacular own goal which blew the alliance apart.



The backlash was enormous and the clubs involved were left having to explain themselves.

Whatever private relationships existed between them before, the Super League made the group far harder to sustain publicly.

There was embarrassment, mistrust and fallout. For a while, the Big Six looked anything but united.

Now they seem to have rediscovered the benefits of acting together when their interests coincide.

That should concern the rest of the Premier League — not because the biggest clubs are doing anything wrong, but because the league has to make sure its collective interests are not simply the sum of the ambitions of its most powerful members.



The danger is that the six biggest voices become so powerful that the other 14 discover their votes are technically equal but politically very different.

The Premier League’s genius has always been that 20 competitors agree to operate one competition.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Its future depends on remembering that the word that matters most in that sentence is not competitors.

It is one.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal sign forward, Enzo Fernandez £120m deal, Alvarez and Barcola latest

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard names the one signing Liverpool must make before deadline day
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard names the one signing Liverpool must make before deadline day

Liverpool had a stuttering start to life under Andoni Iraola against Newcastle and legendary former Reds midfielder Steven Gerrard has given his thoughts on where they can improve

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard has given advice to the Reds ahead of deadline day (Image: Getty Images)

Steven Gerrard believes Liverpool have to sign a new midfielder before the transfer window closes. The Reds have been active in the market this summer ahead of Andoni Iraola’s first season at the helm.

‌



They have signed defender Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, while Ronald Araujo has arrived on loan from Barcelona. Liverpool also remain keen on adding to their attacking options.

‌



A deal is reportedly close for a move for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola, while they have also lodged bids for Brighton wideman Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr.

‌



Despite that, club icon Gerrard has suggested that they need to sign a defensive midfielder before the window slams shut on Tuesday evening. Speaking on TNT Sports, he said: "There's one area that hasn't really had much focus, only really in the last week since the Newcastle game. I believe they need a specialist in the No. 6 position, that's my opinion.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Now, the manager might have different ideas in terms of how he wants the team to look and his philosophy, but I think this team has missed a destroyer, someone who holds the middle of the pitch, who is a massive part of the spine since the team moved Fabinho on.

‌



"I think that position's been sorely missed, I don't think they've got a specialist in that position. That can allow your [Dominik] Szoboszlais and your [Ryan] Gravenberchs and your [Alexis] Mac Allisters to go and join attacks, to make the back four secure. I think they miss that position badly."

There has been some movement when it comes to midfield at Liverpool this summer. Academy graduate Curtis Jones has been sold to Inter Milan, while Harvey Elliott continues to be linked with a move away.

And while Gerrard believes a replacement is needed, he has also suggested that striker also remains a problem position for Iraola. He continued: "Obviously, Ekitike is injured at the moment, so it's a delicate position, the No. 9.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool are on the verge of signing Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

"If there's an issue with Isak, I think there could be problems, especially if rumours are true where [Cody] Gakpo could be going in the opposite direction.

"It's been well reported in the last weeks and months that Liverpool are linked with the wide areas, they're being linked with [Ismaila] Sarr, [Yankuba] Minteh and Bradley Barcola, so they definitely need to strengthen the sides in the forward areas, but also the No. 9 for the what-ifs."

Sports.title: Sky Sports presenter forced to apologise after X-rated Man City live interview
Sports.content:
Sky Sports presenter forced to apologise after X-rated Man City live interview

Rayan Cherki forced Sky Sports to issue a live apology for his comments following Manchester City's win over Crystal Palace

View 2 Images Sky Sports had to apologise after Rayan Cherki swore during his live interview (Image: Sky Sports)

Sky Sports presenter Johnny Phillips was forced to apologise live on air after Rayan Cherki swore in his post-match interview. The Manchester City star scored twice in his side's 4-1 win over Crystal Palace but was not pleased by his first half display.

‌



When asked about his overall performance, he said: "My performance is so-so. In the first half, we didn't find the space, I played s***. When I see Enzo [Maresca] wants to change me, I don't like that. I need to show them I want to play, I want to score. I want to give assists to Erling because today I didn't give him the ball a lot."

‌



Once Cherki stopped talking, Phillips was subsequently forced to apologise for any comments that may have offended anyone watching. Cherki was accompanied by Erling Haaland, who also bagged a brace, in the interview and he appeared to mutter under his breath in response, "I don't think anyone was [offended]."

‌



The comment brought a smile from Cherki, who had been awarded player of the match for his dazzling first goal and impressive second.

When asked if his first strike was one of his best, Cherki shyly said: "I don't know, I just try to give the ball [to Erling]. I'm very happy for the win, see you next week.

Though Cherki did not find Haaland often, he started and then rounded off the rout with Semenyo's cross headed in by the 26-year-old in the first half before he smashed a pass from Phil Foden into the roof of the net late on.

‌



View 2 Images Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland were involved in a chaotic Sky Sports interview (Image: Sky Sports)

The City striker was still keen to heap praise on the Frenchman, though, and interrupted his earlier comments by stating: "Just say what you actually mean, you scored two top goals." Cherki replied while laughing: "That is nothing. I want to give a goal for him."

Haaland later handed the player of the match award to Cherki with the duo joking about the latter being the one who was assisted.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Having picked up the three points, City subsequently sit top of the league after also beating Bournemouth last weekend, though this was a far more convincing display.

Maresca instructed Antoine Semenyo and Phil Foden to stay high and wide while Nico O'Reilly and Josko Gvardiol advanced into midfield. That saw Marc Guehi, Ruben Dias and Abdukodir Khusanov form a back three in possession.

Article continues below

Elsewhere, new signing Ayyoub Bouaddi made his debut off the bench while there were also bright cameos from Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite.

Sports.title: Rayan Cherki runs the show as Man City thump Crystal Palace - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Rayan Cherki runs the show as Man City thump Crystal Palace - 5 talking points

CRYSTAL PALACE 1-4 MAN CITY: Enzo Maresca's side might have spent plenty of cash this summer but it's one of last year's arrivals who is shining in the Premier League

View 3 Images Rayan Cherki was in inspired form at Selhurst Park (Image: Getty Images)

A Rayan Cherki-inspired Manchester City secured a 4-1 victory against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park to extend their perfect start to the season.

‌



After surviving a bright start from the hosts, City took the lead through Erling Haaland. Cherki then doubled their lead with a brilliant individual goal after the break.

‌



Palace found themselves a foothold moments later as Yeremy Pino's free-kick found the net via a touch off of Gianluigi Donnarumma.

‌



But Cherki was not done as he hammered home a brilliant second. Haaland then also doubled his evening's work late on.

City's victory in London leaves new boss Enzo Maresca with a 100 per cent record after two Premier League matches at the helm, while Pierre Sage remains without a point as Palace manager. Here are all of the talking points from Selhurst Park.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Haaland against Palace again

After failing to find the net on the opening day for the first time in his Premier League career, there was no way that Haaland was not scoring at Selhurst Park. After all, the Norwegian sensation had netted at Selhurst Park on every single appearance.

His first goal was very much trademark Haaland, too. Semenyo whipped a brilliant ball into the penalty area, with the striker having escaped his marker to nod a brilliant effort into the back of the net.

Haaland was then on hand late on to latch onto Foden's clever pass and thump a thunderous effort past Dean Henderson.

‌



With three Premier League golden boots to his name, his fight to secure a fourth is well and truly underway.

View 3 Images Haaland has opened his 2026/27 account (Image: Getty Images)

Mixed evening for Foden

City should have been at least 3-0 up come the break but former PFA Player of the Year, Phil Foden, was guilty of missing some more than presentable opportunities.

‌



His first chance came after being picked out by Elliot Anderson, with pretty much the whole goal to aim att but curled his effort high over the crossbar.

His second opportunity came at the end of a flowing move, which saw Nico O'Reilly and Cherki combine. The latter picked out Foden with a brilliant cross but somehow the England man got his header horribly wrong.

Despite that, he still managed to rack up two assists on what was still a productive outing for him.

‌



Cherki brilliance

While Foden struggled in front of goal, he was on hand to tee-up Cherki for what looks to be one of the goals of the season already.

Foden drove into the box and picked out the French playmaker, who showed great feet to dance around three Palace bodies. Just as he looked like he was about to be crowded out, he poked the ball into the far corner with the outside of his foot.

The Frenchman was on the scoresheet again with a stunning drive that flew into the top corner. After his standout debut season in the Premier League, it looks like Cherki is set to be even better this time around.

‌



View 3 Images Cherki has two goals and two assists already this season (Image: Getty Images)

Pinpoint from Pino

Just minutes after City extended their lead, the home side dragged them back as they cut the deficit.

Anderson was somewhat unfortunate to give away a free kick on the edge of the area, which Pino claimed. The Spaniard's effort was precise enough to strike the ball, drop onto the back of City goalkeeper Donnarumma and into the back of the net.

‌



Pino scored just twice in the Premier League last season following a move from Villarreal so will be hoping to improve on those numbers.

Contrasting fortunes for new bosses

It's fair to say that Pierre Sage will have been keen to swap his results for Maresca's. The Frenchman has not had the best start to life at Palace, having lost each of his opening two games.

It's not quite a crisis yet - the Eagles did show some promising signs against City despite the scoreline. But Sage will be hoping to get his first victory sooner rather than later or Palace could find themselves nervously looking over their shoulder.

Article continues below

Maresca in the meantime has won each of his matches as City boss. They don't quite look at their very best quite yet - which is a scary prospect given their display at Selhurst Park - but the results are positive which is all that matters at this stage.

Sports.title: Man City 'ready to rival Arsenal' in transfer race for Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez
Sports.content:
Man City 'ready to rival Arsenal' in transfer race for Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez

Julian Alvarez has been courted by Barcelona and Arsenal in the summer transfer window but now another option has emerged for the Atletico Madrid striker

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez is at the centre of a transfer saga (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Manchester City are reportedly weighing up a move to re-sign Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid in the last few days of the summer transfer window.

‌



Alvarez is the subject of intense transfer speculation following a summer-long saga with Barcelona. Atletico Madrid felt compelled to release a statement this week explaining they will not do business with Barca under any circumstances.

‌



Arsenal are also interested in the Argentina international and have been waiting for developments ahead of the transfer deadline at 11pm on Tuesday night. Alvarez told Atleti he wanted to join Barca, but is now faced with two options: move back to the Premier League or stay in the Spanish capital.

‌



The 26-year-old forward is under contract until June 2030 and is valued at €150million (£128m) by Atleti. They signed him from Manchester City for £81m in August 2024, but now the prospect of a move back to the Etihad Stadium has emerged.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Marca reports that City have 'entered the race' after offloading Omar Marmoush and Savio to Tottenham for what will become a combined £135m when Marmoush's initial loan becomes permanent. The Spanish newspaper notes that Alvarez remains reluctant to return to England and that Atleti would have to find a replacement before agreeing to sell.

‌



Manager Diego Simeone has confirmed that he wants to keep Alvarez, who has skipped training and will not travel with the team to play Sevilla in La Liga this weekend. "From the moment he returns to training, I will do everything I can to make him feel important," said Simeone.

Asked whether Alvarez's situation could be turned around, Simeone added: "As long as you have your health, everything in life can be turned around."

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez is a wanted man (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



"I'm still in the same position, hoping, from a sporting point of view, to be able to help him in the best way so that he continues to be the very important player he is for us," he added.

Alvarez has 49 goals and 17 assists in 107 appearances for Atleti, having previously returned 54 goals and 31 assists in 122 games for City. He left Manchester, in part, to step out of Erling Haaland's shadow and the fact the Norwegian star is still the No.1 striker under Enzo Maresca could put him off returning.

City are also weighing up whether to splash over £120m on Enzo Fernandez following the departures of Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez in recent weeks.

‌



View 3 Images Julian Alvarez was hugely successful at Manchester City, winning multiple honours (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

For Alvarez, everything remains up in the air with four days of the transfer window remaining. But what is certain is that Atleti won't sell to Barcelona.

They said in a statement: "The members of Atlético Madrid's Board of Directors have unanimously expressed their full support for the club's decision not to negotiate the transfer of Julián Alvarez to FC Barcelona. The members of the Board of Directors are aware that:

‌



"Atlético Madrid is open to negotiations that are part of the transfer market, but always in an ethical and professional manner and with respect between clubs.

"We fully support the position previously communicated by the club that FC Barcelona have not met these requirements and, as a result, there have been no negotiations, nor will there be any negotiations with them regarding the transfer of Julián Alvarez."

Sports.title: Gary O'Neil leaps to Matheus Cunha’s defence after Man Utd star's clash with staff member
Sports.content:
Gary O'Neil leaps to Matheus Cunha’s defence after Man Utd star's clash with staff member

Matheus Cunha infamously clashed with a member of the Ipswich Town backroom team during his time with Wolverhampton Wanderers and boss Gary O’Neil has spoken out on the incident

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha is set to be reunited with Gary O'Neil this weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil has leapt to the defence of ‘misunderstood’ Matheus Cunha following his pitch-side clash with a member of staff in 2024. The Brazilian was at the heart of an angry scuffle during his time with Wolverhampton Wanderers.

‌



The brawl, which took place in December 2024, saw a security guard’s glasses broken. Cunha apologised in the aftermath and ahead of being reunited with his former star, Ipswich boss O’Neil has assured that there is no longer an issue.

‌



Speaking ahead of this weekend’s clash with Manchester United, O’Neil said: “Chris [the security guard] is still here! Cunha obviously apologised for that.

‌



“There's always these things going on. I don't think that's a reflection of Matheus as a character at all. I know Chris has forgiven him. Chris has forgiven me for allowing Cunha to do that as well, if it even was my fault.

“Matheus is a good guy, but, like I say, he's playing for Manchester United now and I've got at least 27 people in there that are far further up my importance list than Matheus Cunha anymore. I’m focusing on us.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“I enjoyed my time with Mateus. I’m glad that he's gone on to do well and hopefully we can get one over him at the weekend. Chris's glasses are fine. They might be new ones. We had a good joke about it when I arrived. Chris is a great guy.”

The clash was not the only controversial incident that Cunha was involved in during his time in the Midlands. He was also banned for headbutting Milos Kerkez during an FA Cup clash against Bournemouth.

But O’Neil believes that is not his real character. He added: “He's not that volatile. He's a great guy. He's passionate. I loved working with him. I loved the challenge of teaching him, I suppose, because he was unbelievably raw.

‌



View 2 Images Cunha sparked the clash back in December 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

“Not technically, he was unbelievably good technically. But his tactical stuff and his understanding of what the team needed from him, I felt needed a lot of work.

“We spent a lot of time together trying to help him understand how we can be better for the team, and he committed to it. He was fantastic for us.

‌



“Obviously, a big, big positive from our time at Wolves was the work done with him. He got a big move off the back of that work. He's maybe misunderstood. I wouldn't describe him as volatile at all. I think he's a good guy.

“He wears his heart on his sleeve. I suppose the game can sometimes take you to places emotionally. I'll have done things that maybe you wouldn't do again. It's just the nature of the game and the nature of the Premier League. But he's a good guy.

“I think a lot of him, we still stay in contact, but I'm desperate to beat him and send him a cheeky late night Sunday text saying, ‘unlucky Matheus’. That would be nice.”

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk sends ‘unacceptable’ message to Liverpool teammates after slow start
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk sends ‘unacceptable’ message to Liverpool teammates after slow start

Liverpool had a slow start to life under Andoni Iraola following the Spanish coach’s arrival at Anfield and captain Virgil van Dijk has had his say on the club’s new approach

View 2 Images Van Dijk has called for improvement from his Liverpool teammates (Image: Getty Images)

Virgil van Dijk has explained that Liverpool might take time to get used to Andoni Iraola’s approach after an ‘unacceptable’ season. The Reds had a tricky second campaign under Arne Slot, finishing fifth in the Premier League before the Dutchman was sacked.

‌



Liverpool moved for ex-Bournemouth coach Iraola. But the Spaniard has had a slow start to life at Anfield, the Reds having drawn 2-2 with Newcastle on the opening day.

‌



Speaking ahead of their first home game of the season against Nottingham Forest on Saturday afternoon, Van Dijk has suggested that it might take time for Liverpool to be back to their best after an ‘unacceptable’ campaign last term.

‌



"When you have a new coach with new plans and new ideas, it is always going to take a bit of time to put those into practice," Van Dijk wrote in his programme notes.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"But it is down to us to do that as quickly as we can. I can tell you that we are working extremely hard every day on the training ground, because we all want to improve, we want to be better and more consistent.

"We want to win, ultimately. At Liverpool, that should always be the aim. You don't need me to tell you that last season was tough, unacceptable in my opinion. We are better than that, much better in fact, and now we need to show it."

Van Dijk has also given his take on Liverpool’s upcoming assignment, having named four non-negotiables that his teammates need to show in the game if they want to stand any chance of securing victory.

‌



View 2 Images Van Dijk in action against Newcastle on the opening day (Image: Getty Images)

He added: "Like I say, we showed some good things against Newcastle. St. James' Park is always a tough place to go, and though obviously we were not happy with the goals we conceded.

"I think we showed good character to twice come back and we worked extremely hard as a team to take something from the game. It wasn't a victory, which is what we wanted of course, but it was a deserved point in my opinion, and we take that and move on.

‌



"This will be another tough game, make no mistake. We know how dangerous Nottingham Forest can be, and we will need to perform at our best if we want to get the three points.

"Again, it starts with the basics; togetherness, hard work, desire and commitment. If we have those – and we will – then we will give ourselves the best possible chance to show our quality and get the result we all want."

Sports.title: Scheffler chases Hovland at Tour Championship as McIlroy's hopes fade
Sports.content:
Viktor Hovland holds a share of the lead at the halfway stage of the PGA Tour's season-ending Tour Championship, with Scottie Scheffler firmly in FedExCup contention.

Hovland - the 2023 FedExCup champion - birdied the par-five last to post a second-round 66 at East Lake Golf Club, pulling him level on 10 under alongside American Ryan Gerard.

Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup posted matching 67s to sit one back in Atlanta, while Cameron Young fired a round-of-the-day 62 to charge from joint-bottom of the leaderboard to within two of the lead.

Image: Tour Championship

Young is joined on eight under by Scheffler, who made five birdies in a seven-hole stretch around the turn during a three-under 67, with English duo Justin Rose and Matt Fitzpatrick three adrift alongside Ludvig Åberg and Adam Scott.

A congested leaderboard sees 19 of the 29-man field separated by just five shots, but defending champion Tommy Fleetwood is six behind on four under and three-time FedExCup winner Rory McIlroy a further stroke back.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy title hopes suffered a big setback with a double-bogey at the par-four third

How Hovland moved into FedExCup mix

Young was first out on his own but quickly charged up the leaderboard with five birdies in six holes from the third, before starting his back nine with successive birdies to move within one behind overnight leader Min Woo Lee.

The Players champion bogeyed the next and went on a run of pars until a sensational finish at the par-five last, where a 40-foot eagle set the clubhouse target, as Lee immediately lost ground with a three-putt triple-bogey at the par-four fifth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Young closed out a stunning second-round 62 with a long-range eagle at the par-five last

Gerard had started three back and fell further behind with a bogey at the first, but he followed back-to-back birdies from the third by adding two more from the seventh to charge into a share of the lead.

Playing partner Bhatia was already in that logjam on eight under after three birdies in four holes from the fourth, while Burns and Woodland - playing several groups ahead - both picked up a shot at the 13th to briefly make it a five-way tie.

Image: Ryan Gerard

Gerard started his back nine by matching Bhatia's birdie and held the solo lead when his playing partner bogeyed the 12th, only for Gotterup to race through the field and briefly pull level on nine under after a birdie at the 13th.

Hovland was three behind until he registered birdies at the 10th and 12th by nailing a 25-footer at the par-three 15th, putting him alongside Gerard, with Scheffler one back until a careless approach led to a dropped shot at the 17th.

Image: Viktor Hovland, of Norway, plays a shot on the first hole during the second round of the Tour Championship

Gerard produced a brilliant up and down to close a second-round 65 with a birdie and move to 10 under, as Hovland followed a key 12-foot par save at the 16th by rolling in from 10 feet at the last to move joint-top of the leaderboard.

"I found something that seems to be going straight, so very happy with that," Hovland told reporters. "Last week I drove it awful. The week before, not so great either. It's not like I've changed too much since those last few weeks, but I'm driving it better this week. You've just got to take advantage of it!

More to follow...

Sports.title: Wrexham's winless start continues with defeat to Birmingham
Sports.content:
Wrexham's winless start to the season was extended to four games in all competitions after they were beaten 2-1 by Birmingham at the Racecourse Ground.

Centre-back Phil Neumann - who has never scored more than two goals in a single season - scored both Blues goals, either side of a Callum Doyle equaliser.

It was the ideal response from Chris Davies' side, following their 6-1 hammering at the hands of Brentford in the Carabao Cup in midweek.

Image: Phil Neumann's double won the game for Birmingham

Wrexham's winless start August 7: Middlesbrough 1-0 Wrexham (Carabao Cup)

August 17: Cardiff 1-1 Wrexham

August 22: Wrexham 1-1 Watford

August 28: Wrexham 1-2 Birmingham

The Blues deservedly established a lead after 13 minutes, when Neumann headed in Alex Cochrane's header at the far post, but few could deny it should have been 3-0 at the break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Birmingham's Phil Neumann puts them into the lead against Wrexham with a close-range header.

Before the opener, Ollie Rathbone was in the right place at the right time to block August Priske's header from point-blank range, while after it, Jay Stansfield stepped on to Carlos Vicente's neat cut-back and inexplicably powered a shot past the right-hand post when it looked easier to score.

Wrexham generated just 0.22 xG in the first half, but came out with more bite after the break and were rewarded when Lewis O'Brien's dipping cross was helped past James Beadle by Callum Doyle.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Doyle draws his side level against Birmingham for Wrexham.

But the lead lasted less than 10 minutes. Priske launched a long throw in from the right and recycled it when the first delivery was cleared, finding Neumann, who glanced a header past Anthony Patterson.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Phil Neumann heads home another goal to double his goal tally and put his side in the lead again.

Wrexham upped the tempo as the final whistle approached, but they could not find the goal that would have haunted Birmingham.

7: OFF THE LINE ! August Priske has the goal gaping in front of him, but he heads at Wrexham's Ollie Rathbone.

! August Priske has the goal gaping in front of him, but he heads at Wrexham's Ollie Rathbone. 13: GOAL ! Alex Cochrane sends an inswinging corner to the far post, where Phil Neumann heads over the line from close range.

! Alex Cochrane sends an inswinging corner to the far post, where Phil Neumann heads over the line from close range. 23: HUGE MISS ! Carlos Vicente chops the ball to Jay Stansfield on his right after an overload, but the forward blasts over the bar.

! Carlos Vicente chops the ball to Jay Stansfield on his right after an overload, but the forward blasts over the bar. 37: SAVE ! Wrexham's best chance of the first half. Danny Imray drives in from the right, with his deflected shot well saved by a diving James Beadle.

! Wrexham's best chance of the first half. Danny Imray drives in from the right, with his deflected shot well saved by a diving James Beadle. 54: GOAL ! Lewis O'Brien's brilliant cross dips perfectly for Callum Doyle to equalise.

! Lewis O'Brien's brilliant cross dips perfectly for Callum Doyle to equalise. 63: GOAL ! Priske recycles a clearance and finds Neumann, who glances in his second of the night.

! Priske recycles a clearance and finds Neumann, who glances in his second of the night. 77: SO CLOSE! Let-off for Birmingham. Kieffer Moore's header is not held by James Beadle and only some brave defending from Christoph Klarer prevents a killer Wrexham connection.

Parkinson bemoans "softest two goals conceded in all my time at Wrexham"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson says the goals his side conceded in defeat to Birmingham were worse than any goal they've conceded during his time in charge - including in the National League.

Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson speaking on Sky Sports:

"The two goals we conceded are two of the softest goals we've conceded in all my time here - and that includes being in the National League. You can't concede goals like that and expect to win a game of football.

"You've got to defend the box - it's as simple as that - in any division, but particularly the Championship we've got to defend our box better, head the ball out, defend set-plays.

"I thought we lacked conviction in our play tonight in the first half, I've got to be honest. Second half, I thought we were better, got the goal back, and that's why I'm so annoyed with the second goal because we'd started really well, got back in the game.

"We almost looked like a team of everyone looking around the pitch for someone else to go and make it happen, rather than taking responsibility as individuals.

"In football, you can't feel sorry for yourself and I felt we looked like that tonight for some reason. You cannot feel sorry for yourself because no one else is going to help you, you can only help yourself. We've got to look long and hard at ourselves and come out fighting at Millwall."

Davies: We looked like a team

Birmingham manager Chris Davies speaking on Sky Sports:

"It was a really good night for us. I thought we started the game really well, just like you want to away from home. We got on the front foot, had some moments we could've been maybe a couple of goals up at half-time, so I was really pleased with that.

"I think we looked like a team, that's the main thing. We looked like a real team, and we had to be to come to a place like Wrexham and play a really solid, really good side, especially at home. It's a big, big win."

Do Wrexham need to sign more players before Deadline Day?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jobi McAnuff and Gary Rowett believe Wrexham need to enter the transfer market for more 'physical' players to aid in their league campaign after a winless start this season.

Jobi McAnuff on Sky Sports Football:

"They possibly need a more dominant centre-half, which is something they had during that run through the leagues they had.

"Looking at tonight [2-1 defeat to Birmingham] sometimes it takes a performance or scenarios like this to maybe jog the hierarchy.

"One thing I'm sure Phil Parkinson will say is that he's been backed to the hilt by that ownership group in terms of what he feels he needs to move the club on.

"I'm sure they will feel there's enough there, but I'm sure with Phil, questions will be getting asked in the next few days."

Sports.title: Greaves denied by Cross in last-leg thriller on European Tour debut
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves took Rob Cross to a last-leg decider before losing out 6-5 on her European Tour debut in the first round of the Hungarian Darts Trophy.

Rising star Greaves, 22, made history by becoming the first woman to compete in a PDC European Tour event after qualifying last month for both this weekend's event in Budapest and the Czech Darts Open in September.

And she pushed the experienced Cross to a deciding 11th leg in a thrilling tie on Friday evening, averaging an impressive match-best of 104.88.

Cross, who played well himself with an 101.9 average, had made a flying start to the match with a 170 first-leg checkout but Greaves, who is dominating the PDC women's series, quickly showed her competitiveness and took the next two legs.

She moved one more leg away from victory at 5-4 but Cross hit back to win the final two legs, with Greaves left to rue mistakes with her first two darts when left with 70 in the decider.

Image: Rob Cross is eyeing his first European Tour title since 2024

Cross seized his first chance at victory by taking out 61, with the 35-year-old to now play Luke Woodhouse in Saturday's second round.

Earlier on Friday evening and Hungary's own Laszlo Kadar had caused the upset of the night by beating Daryl Gurney 6-5. Kadar will now play Jonny Clayton in Saturday's second round.

Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen and Michael van Gerwen all enter the tournament in round two.

Sports.title: 'I need competition' - Alcaraz returns from injury in time for US Open defence
Sports.content:
"I need competition."

Carlos Alcaraz says he is "feeling great" as he prepares for his US Open defence in what will be the Spaniard's first appearance since recovering from a right wrist injury sustained in April.

Alcaraz's long absence has clouded his prospects, but the seven-time Grand Slam champion has built a reputation for producing his best tennis on the grandest stages and cannot ‌be discounted despite the uncertainty surrounding his return.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams walked out to an incredible atmosphere at the US Open Mixed Doubles Championship

He will launch his title defence against Russia's Roman Safiullin following a quick tune-up alongside Serena Williams in the mixed doubles.

"I'm feeling very good, and I think that injury helped me a lot to understand that right now, everything is in my head. I have to trust my team, trust the people who tell me that everything is going to be fine," said the 23-year-old.

"So I just have to go 100 per cent. Right now, with the training I've done so far, everything has gone well. I'm trying to get away from that fear and play normally."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner from the US Open final in 2025

'I haven't changed anything technically'

There were fears Alcaraz may have had to tinker with the playing style in order to stop the problem from flaring up again - Britain's Jack Draper attempted to change his serve in a bid to get over his injury problems but remains frustratingly on the sidelines.

But Alcaraz insists he just needs competitive action.

"I haven't changed anything. I've been doing the same things. I haven't changed anything technically, in terms of my movements or the way I'm going to play," he said.

"I just wanted to feel that I was going to be myself. I knew that coming here to the US Open, being a best-of-five-set tournament and being my first tournament after such a long time, was going to be a huge challenge.

"Probably, in terms of preparation, it wasn't the ideal time. But my team and I believe that I'm ready. It wasn't an easy decision. I did everything I needed to do to be ready. I tried to do everything perfectly, both on and off the court, to feel prepared.

"We saw that everything was fine, that everything was responding properly, and we believed it was the right time to come back."

Alcaraz also admitted it is "weird" that he has not seen injured world No 1 Jannik Sinner in several months, saying: "It's a weird situation to be honest. I just wish him all the best... a great recovery and to see him back in court at his best."

'A lifetime experience' watching Spain win World Cup

Image: Spain lifted the World Cup in New York this summer

Alcaraz was not entirely out of the limelight during his time away from the court, after carrying the World Cup trophy onto the pitch at the MetLife Stadium before Spain's win over Argentina.

"For me it was a lifetime experience, seeing Spain winning the World Cup," he said.

"Louis Vuitton had the trunks that was carrying the trophy, so they told me that I'm down to do it. And, I mean, it was a lifetime experience for me, like holding the trophy in the ceremony, to give it to them, you know, on the field. So it was a great experience."

Sports.title: Penge storms ahead on second rain-hit day at British Masters
Sports.content:
Marco Penge leads by two shots midway through the second round of the rain-affected Husqvarna British Masters after another day of stormy weather at The Belfry.

After three suspensions of play on Thursday had delayed the completion of the event's first round, play restarted early on Friday morning in Sutton Coldfield with half the field resuming their opening rounds before the rest soon got theirs under way.

Play continued until 2.29pm when itplay was suspended for thunder and lightning, which caused a delay of two hours and 11 minutes before action could resume again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Marco Penge produces a masterclass at the British Masters with this eagle on the 10th at The Belfry

Penge was among the players to both play his full first round and then start his second on Friday, completing a mammoth 32 holes in total.

He shot a three-under 69 for his first round but his second round was immediately turbocharged when, starting on the back nine, he drove the 302-yard 10th and then sunk his 11-foot putt for eagle.

Although he bogeyed the par-four 13th, Penge hit back with birdies at the 14th, 16th and 17th to go out in 32.

He quickly followed that run with further birdies at the first, second, third and fifth holes before play was suspended for the day at 7.50pm.

Speaking earlier after the completion of his first round, Penge said of his start: "It's solid. Pretty tough conditions with the wind and with the back flags, the greens being so soft, it's tough to hit it close. Bogey-free round is always nice.

"My body should be fine. I obviously just had two weeks off and haven't played that much the last couple of months. I'm pretty fresh compared to the other lads. I've got my physio and my trainer here."

Penge leads New Zealand's Daniel Hillier, who was six under through 14 holes, by two shots with England's Matthew Jordan currently tied for third on seven under. Jordan is one under for his second round with four holes to play.

Jordan had finished the elongated opening second one shot behind Spain's Nacho Elvira, who had led the way with a seven-under 65.

Early Thursday front-runner Tom McKibbin, who finished at four under, is also yet to start his second round.

Organisers confirmed that players will be back on the course to restart the second round at 7.30am on Saturday morning. Players yet to start their second round will then tee off between 8.45am and 10.45am.

Round three will be a two-tee start and will not begin before 4pm.

Also, the last five newly-promoted teams to play their first home game of the season have won it, so history is certainly pointing towards a positive afternoon for Coventry. There is also a betting-system angle that makes me reluctant to write off the visitors. Tottenham vs Newcastle United, Saturday 5:30pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 HERE!

There are times in betting when you have to decide whether a bad performance is a warning sign or a price-making opportunity.

I'm leaning towards the latter with Tottenham.

The 3-0 defeat at Brentford was awful. There is no dressing it up. Spurs looked disjointed, physically behind the game and defensively vulnerable, while Roberto De Zerbi admitted afterwards that his side were "not a team" yet.

But I'm prepared to give them another chance.

De Zerbi has an excellent record in the game immediately following a defeat of three or more goals, winning eight of 11 such matches, with his teams averaging 2.1 goals. That's a big enough sample to make me sit up as Tottenham are available at 6/5 with Sky Bet. It's a bet.

Spurs had five competitive debutants in their starting XI, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro were unavailable and several players had either returned late from the World Cup or endured disrupted pre-seasons.

It doesn't excuse the performance, but it does suggest that some of what went wrong is fixable.

And there is now a sense of the cavalry returning.

I'm not suddenly convinced Spurs are back to being the team many expected them to be before a ball was kicked. But the home win price looks quite tasty at odds-against as this feels like a classic reaction game for De Zerbi and Tottenham.

Are Chelsea now structurally a team capable of producing these types of matches regularly? I'd be confident of that answer being yes, meaning there is value in backing their games to be high scoring before the market full adjusts.

There is something about this fixture that makes me think we could be in for another game where both managers are more interested in avoiding defeat than throwing bodies forward. The draw and under 2.5 goals is 100/30 with Sky Bet and that's a price worth respecting.

Everyone quite rightly came away from Fulham's 3-2 defeat to Chelsea talking about Cole Palmer.

But what about Josh King?

The Fulham teenager was not too far behind Palmer in the wow-factor stakes.

King scored Fulham's first goal at Craven Cottage. He finished the game with three shots, two on target and was a constant threat for a Fulham side that looked dangerous in transition. Manchester United vs Ipswich, Sunday 4:30pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 HERE!

You don't have to convince me twice to back a set-piece angle.

Manchester United won just 42 per cent of their duels in their 2-0 defeat to Hull - the lowest figure recorded by any Premier League team on the opening weekend. That lack of physical bite is a concern in a league where you simply cannot afford to be second best in the fundamentals.

Since Michael Carrick took charge, United have conceded 20 Premier League goals in 18 matches - 10 of them from set plays. That's an extraordinary ratio. Only Bournemouth and Leeds have conceded a higher proportion of their goals from set-pieces during that period.

And Hull provided the perfect example of how to exploit it, scoring both goals from dead-ball situations in their stunning victory at Old Trafford.

So why should we expect Ipswich to be any different?

Dara O'Shea is the first-contact man on set pieces for Town and averaged 0.95 shots per 90 over the last 12 months. That's a great number for a defender and tells us something about how aggressive Ipswich are in targeting him. He is Evens for at least one shot and 18/1 to score with Sky Bet.

Sports.title: Cherki and Haaland double up in Manchester City cruise at Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
All who attend the Rayan Cherki show know the ticket comes with a guarantee of entertainment. Enzo Maresca, a manager famed for his obsessive positional control, does not need to put limits on the Manchester City wizard. Cherki has to feel free and he was at his creative best against Crystal Palace, who were in this game before City’s creative heartbeat took it away from them in the second half.

It has been a fine start to the former Lyon player’s second year in England. Cherki was inspired against Bournemouth last week, coming off the bench to spark City’s fightback from 1-0 down with two assists, and this was better. The Frenchman scored twice and the first, a little prod with the outside of his left foot after a mazy run, left you wondering if you have seen something like it before.

Palace, stuck on zero points despite fleeting signs of encouragement in Pierre Sage’s first two outings, had no answer to Cherki’s magic. He is an irrepressible talent and a deep thinker. Listening to the post-match plaudits, Cherki smiled, shrugged and said his performance in the first half was “so shit”. Maresca, though, had a different view.

“His performance for me was very good, not because of the two goals, but the way he worked off the ball,” City’s manager said. “He has to press. His game was complete. He loves football. We know how good he is. We know the quality he has.”

Cherki was not alone in starring for City. Phil Foden impressed and Erling Haaland, who is up and running for the season, grabbed an emphatic double in a performance strong enough to make Maresca think his post-Pep team have moved on from their Community Shield debacle. “We struggled the first five, 10 minutes, because we were pressing in the wrong way,” the Italian said. “After that we were in control.”

A challenge for Maresca is working with an incomplete midfield after the exits of Rodri and Bernardo Silva. Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived from Lille, £86m an eye-catching fee for an 18-year-old after his exploits for Morocco at the World Cup, but there is room for one more. Enzo Fernández, desperate to leave Chelsea, is the top target before Tuesday’s deadline.

Not that anyone is going to argue that City are short on midfield options. Maresca, ever the tinkerer, shuffled the pack again. The experiment with Marc Guéhi in the engine room was discontinued, allowing him to slot into central defence against his old side. The £116m Elliot Anderson was the sole pivot, Nico O’Reilly pushed high in a 4-1-4-1 system and Josko Gvardiol inverted from left-back, much like Marc Cucurella in Maresca’s Chelsea side.

There are subtle tweaks to the Guardiola template, though some things never change. City led through a familiar source in the 17th minute, Antoine Semenyo crossing from the left and Haaland finding space to loop a clever header over Dean Henderson.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland wraps up victory with the fourth goal. Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images

The defending was poor from Palace, who have had an uncertain summer. They were arranged in familiar fashion, Sage sticking with Oliver Glasner’s 3-4-2-1, but some key faces have gone and others were missing.

Jørgen Strand Larsen led the line in the absence of the unsettled Jean-Philippe Mateta, who may be out for four weeks. Ismaïla Sarr, keen to join Galatasaray, was unavailable and Daniel Muñoz was on the bench amid suggestions of interest from Nottingham Forest. Frailties were inevitable. The defence has lost Maxence Lacroix, sold to Chelsea. Anderson, Semenyo and Foden had chances before half-time. “You saw how we want to play until the 65th minute,” Sage said. “We trust in our process.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sage likes to play on the front foot. Adam Wharton, subject of a failed enquiry from City recently, swept a ball through for Eddie Nketiah to test Gianluigi Donnarumma in the second minute. Daichi Kamada went close and Tyrick Mitchell fluffed a header after more enterprising play from Wharton.

Palace lacked incision, Nketiah missing again early in the second half. City pressed, O’Reilly and Foden hustling Kamada. Foden advanced and Cherki took over. The Frenchman danced in from the left, danger rising as he wriggled into the area. A host of Palace defenders were thrown off balance, unable to live with Cherki’s footwork and close control. Expect the unexpected. Cherki floated past Jaydee Canvot and held off Chris Richards. For a moment the ball seemed stuck under his feet but he used Takehiro Tomiyasu as a shield and unveiled a finish that was less poke and more dab, Henderson rooted to the spot as the ball rolled tantalisingly over the line.

Palace quickly grabbed a lifeline, Yéremy Pino’s free-kick hitting the woodwork and bouncing in off Donarumma for an own goal, but Cherki was in his element. He scored again in the 59th minute, a fierce shot from 20 yards deceiving Henderson after flicking off Richards.

City sent Bouaddi on for his debut, Anderson withdrawn. They wanted more. Foden, catching the eye in front of Thomas Tuchel, released Haaland. The Norwegian, who has scored in all six of his league games against Palace, was never going to miss.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola tells Liverpool’s forwards to ‘exhaust themselves’
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has said it is more important for Liverpool’s forwards to exhaust themselves than perform for 90 minutes as he prepares to make an “emotional” Premier League bow at Anfield.

The Liverpool head coach hopes his attacking options will be improved by the arrival of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and another winger before Tuesday’s deadline, with only Victor Muñoz added to his front line so far. The Basque coach has outlined the demands he will put on his forwards as they adapt to a new era at Liverpool.

Iraola said: “For me, wingers, forwards, I always tell them that they don’t need to give us 90 minutes. I tell them it is good news when they are exhausted because then we have taken everything from you and someone else will come in.

“We have the situation now with Jérémy [Jacquet], who hasn’t had a proper pre-season but he is close to getting there. But normally defenders can last 90 minutes easier. For offensive players, it’s not mandatory that you play the whole game. Once you are done, we can change you. I think it’s the best way, and they all have to understand it like this.”

Iraola said Muñoz was “ready to start games” having missed the opening weeks of pre-season as he recuperated from Spain’s victorious World Cup campaign. The 23-year-old impressed from the bench at Newcastle last weekend and was signed for £34.5m from Osasuna on Iraola’s recommendation.
