Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I had never coached against Victor because he made his debut in La Liga when I was already here in the Premier League but I had very good references of him,” Iraola said. “The club put his name [to me] and we started to analyse his game. We all liked what he gives us. It’s early for him in terms of him not being able to speak the language, and he needs to get a better relationship with teammates, but I like his attitude. He works very hard. He is ready to play right side, left side, and he impacted the game the other day. The subs all played very well.”

Iraola’s wife and two young children will be at Anfield on Saturday – as will the club’s new vice-chair, Amit Bhatia – to witness his first competitive home game, against Nottingham Forest.

“My wife never normally comes to my games,” he said. “But now she is starting to go because my kids want to go. The kids are starting to understand football a little bit and they will sometimes go. Not all the time, but they will be there for the first game because the timing is very good.

“I think there will be an emotional part that is going to be probably only for me. I know it’s my first game but I will not be trying to think too much about those things. Probably when the game finishes, and if it finishes well, then I will be more thinking of myself.”

Sports.title: Premier League news: David Moyes unsettled by Manchester City’s interest in Iliman Ndiaye
Sports.content:
1. City’s Ndiaye bid unsettles Moyes David Moyes has responded to Manchester City’s interest in Iliman Ndiaye by insisting Everton do not have enough time to reinvest money raised through player sales before the transfer deadline. The Everton manager is determined to add to his squad before Tuesday’s deadline, not lose one of his better players such as Ndiaye, with the club still attempting to end their lengthy search for a new right-back. In contrast to the Everton chief executive, Angus Kinnear, who recently claimed the club were planning to challenge for Europe this season, Moyes insisted the squad needs “a lot of work” before it can achieve that target. City have yet to bid for Ndiaye, who has three years remaining on his Everton contract but declined several offers of an extension last season as they did not include a release clause for a Champions League club. “I think it would be very difficult to get it reinvested if anything came in, we are getting into a really late period now,” said Moyes, speaking of player sales in general. On Ndiaye, he added: “I’m certainly not encouraging a bid. I’m not encouraging that in a million years. I don’t know if it would be too tight for time. Deals and contracts are taking much longer now. There seems to be a lot more involved.” Everton remain interested in City’s Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but a right-back and centre-forward are more of a priority. Moyes added: “I’m saying there’s not much time but I’ll still try to see what we can do. I think we need to do much more if possible. We’re 100% trying to get a right-back and we will try and do that right up until the end of the window.” Everton’s positive start has been tainted by tensions created by Kinnear’s claims that The Friedkin Group, the club’s owners, viewed last season as “a failure” by missing out on European football and that Europe is achievable this term despite only modest investment in Moyes’s team. In response to the latter claim, Moyes said: “There would be a lot of work to do to put us in that category, but nobody put us in that category last year and for most of the season we ran close. You never know. We have started the season well and players have started the games good so that gives me hope that it could be a possibility.” Andy Hunter

2. Milan fixture a riposte to Magpies, says Le Bris Régis Le Bris has said Sunderland’s forthcoming trip to Milan in the Europa League is “a symbol” of the club’s upward trajectory. For many years Newcastle fans have taunted their local rivals with chants of “You’ll never see a Mackem in Milan” and, after arriving from Brittany two years ago, Le Bris swiftly learned that St James’ Park regulars regarded themselves as distinctly superior to Sunderland supporters. Now, though, the tables have turned and Le Bris is enjoying the moment. Sunderland’s manager agreed that it seemed somehow appropriate that the first fixture involving his team to be drawn in Monaco on Friday featured a trip to San Siro. “To get back in Europe with this fixture, it’s a symbol,” said Le Bris, whose side finished seventh in the Premier League last season after beating Newcastle home and away. “It’s iconic. Milan is a massive club and it’s a massive story. “I’m aware of it [the Newcastle fans’ Milan jibes], but I want to speak more about us. We are proud to be in Sunderland and our fans deserve to be in this position. It’s [going to be] a huge experience and we are very proud to be part of it but we want to be efficient. We want to be competitive in the Europa League.” As Sunderland fans began ordering T-shirts and sweatshirts emblazoned with the message “Mackem in Milan” to wear in northern Italy, Le Bris seemed delighted that three players, goalkeeper Robin Roefs, winger Romaine Mundle and the forward Wilson Isidor have signed new long-term contracts at the Stadium of Light. Newcastle fans in Milan in 2023. One of the banners shown says: ‘Have you ever seen a Mackem in Milan?’ Photograph: PA Wire/PA “They see their future in Sunderland because they trust the club and like the environment and they trust the ambition of the club,” said a manager whose side will also face AZ, Dinamo Zagreb, Levski Sofia and Jagiellonia at the Stadium of Light and Anderlecht, Lech Poznan and Torreense away in the Europa League. Le Bris, whose team are at home to Fulham on Sunday, declined to comment on Sunderland’s attempt to sign Jack Grealish on loan from Manchester City but it is believed the former England winger is now most likely to rejoin Everton. Sunderland, meanwhile, remain in the hunt for a right winger and a striker this summer. “I trust the recruitment staff,” said Le Bris. “We are well aligned about the targets we need to make the team better and I still think that we will succeed in the transfer market.” Louise Taylor

3. Gonzalez ‘a smart player with huge potential’ Matthias Jaissle is convinced new arrival Nico González will not take long to hit the ground running after his big-money arrival from Manchester City. The Spaniard could make his Newcastle debut on Saturday at Tottenham after a move from City that could rise to £52m this week, with the head coach excited by the 24-year-old’s ceiling. “He trained with us and he looks sharp,” Jaissle said. “It will take time [to adapt] and I can not tell you how long it takes but he’s a smart player, he has huge potential and already brings so much quality in the squad. He will adapt fast into our way of playing and then we can enjoy.” View image in fullscreen Nico González is presented to the Newcastle fans at St James’ Park: ‘He will adapt fast into our way of playing,’ says Matthias Jaissle. Photograph: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United/Getty Images Jaissle is hopeful that Gonzalez will not be the last player through the door at St James’ Park in this summer’s window, with the Belgium wideman Matias Fernandez-Pardo tipped to move to Tyneside from Lille. “It’s the first message of the morning – to push,” Jaissle said. “The management and Ross [Wilson], the sporting director, they’re doing an amazing job, trying everything. “We want to be smart, we don’t want to act in panic, so I’m really optimistic things will happen.” PA Media

4. Glasner wants to bolster squad after Delap deal Oliver Glasner expects more signings at Nottingham Forest after the arrival of the striker Liam Delap. The 23-year-old joined from Chelsea for a club-record £45m fee on Thursday, and Glasner plans to make further additions before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. Glasner would not comment on a reported £22m Forest offer for his former Crystal Palace wing-back Daniel Muñoz, but the Austrian did admit prospective deals were close to completion. “I think we will add two players,” Glasner said before Saturday’s trip to Liverpool and on the back of home league and Carabao Cup defeats by Leeds. “One we have added, that means we will have at least one more signing. Close deals, quite close to be done, but now from today our focus is on the Liverpool match. That is the most important thing in the next 30 hours and then we have three more days to get the deals over the line.” View image in fullscreen Liam Delap is looking to reignite his career at the City Ground after being frozen out at Chelsea. Photograph: Ritchie Sumpter/Nottingham Forest FC/Getty Images Delap left Chelsea after scoring only two goals in all competitions following his move from Ipswich last summer, and was made to train away from the first-team squad by new Blues manager Xabi Alonso. Glasner said: “It is clear you have to look for a club where you have better chances to get minutes and reignite your career, and that is why we think we are the right club for him.” PA Media

5. O’Neil not finished in transfer market Gary O’Neil has insisted Ipswich are not finished in the transfer window after another busy week at the Premier League newcomers. Argentina international and World Cup winner Exequiel Palacios arrived at Portman Road on Thursday in the latest big-money move secured by the Suffolk club. Talks remain ongoing with the Aston Vila forward Tammy Abraham, who is yet to make a decision on whether to join on a season-long loan, it is understood, but O’Neil is hopeful more can occur in the coming days. Before Sunday’s trip to Manchester United, O’Neil told a press conference: “No, nothing to report on that [Abraham move]. We’re hopefully not finished. We’re still trying to do some business. As to who that is or what positions that will be in, there’s no update from me. “We’re still working hard to try and improve the group, but my focus now is firmly on the game at the weekend and making sure that we’re fully prepared for what is going to be an incredibly tough test.” Ipswich could have Florentino Luís involved at Old Trafford and Palacios is set to make his debut. Azor Matusiwa and Jack Taylor remain sidelined. PA Media

Sports.title: Cartoon alpaca Cole Palmer is a unicorn in this world inventing moments of pure pleasure | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
This week Central Cee launched his new Premier League song, called The Team. It owes its existence to a youth-centred, fist-bumping corporate tie-in with Coca-Cola, the press release for which appears to have involved a man in golf-casual clothing frowning at his computer screen for half an hour before typing “cool urban street words, what are?” into the AI search box, then nipping off for a quick brain-bowl strategy lunch with Roger from the Bluesky Synergy hub.

The song is really good, because Central Cee is really good. He’s super-smart with words, funny and snappy, but also surprisingly tender and raw.

And yes, this is an oh-no-dad’s-talking-about-rap moment. You can just scroll down if you like. The whole thing moves on to Cole Palmer very quickly, why he’s both the best English footballer and very easy to love currently, for various reasons.

Central Cee is a significant figure, perhaps the biggest British recording artist right now. He’s also oddly raw and fearless in the things he says, in a way that feels distinct from the standard, mannered modern person, and which has got him into trouble at least once.

A few years back there was a furore when Central Cee decided to speak out against sexual prejudice. This sounds as if it should just be fine. Except, Central Cee’s call for tolerance was expressed via a lyric in the song Doja. And that lyric was: “How can I be homophobic? My bitch is gay.”

Hmm. Problems there. What Central Cee is saying here, what Central Cee has done while appearing to express a progressive sensibility, is to introduce an entirely new tier of … Basically what he’s saying is: how can I be homophobic? I’m far too busy being sexist.

This caused understandable offence. The b-word is demeaning and cheap, whatever your intentions. Don’t say it. Find better words. To his credit, Central Cee was very good at explaining and apologising, open to other views, while also seeming genuinely non-judgmental of other people regardless of difference or identity, with the exception, of course, of wastemen, mugs and snitches.

He seems to have been forgiven now. More than that, he’s startlingly successful, the most streamed British rap artist of all time. Young people respond to him hungrily. He seems adaptive, fitted to the modern world. In the Coke video he looks blankly into the lens, gives you everything and nothing, risky but also weirdly fearless.

What does this have to do with Cole Palmer, and the surge of heartfelt Palmer-love across all platforms this week after his brilliant performance against Fulham on Monday?

First, Palmer is good friends with Central Cee. He even turned up at the launch of the Coke song just before Chelsea’s Premier League opener. And Palmer really was sensational at Craven Cottage, twirling about between the defensive lines, all perfect touch and interesting angles.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer was sensational for Chelsea against Fulham at Craven Cottage. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The reaction was significant too. Everyone went wild for this. In particular passionate football men of a certain age went wild. This boy is gold, this boy gets people off their seats, the man in the TalkSport video chair growled, speaking from the gut and the spleen, coming off less like a piece of football analysis, more like a man offering a brave, husky funeral elegy for a very loyal family dog.

This passion does have an edge to it. It is a mark of how hungry we are for something different, a counterpoint to the dominance of systems football, that despite being entirely academy-coded Palmer still seems to be a unicorn in this world.

For the middle-aged proper football man he can look like a flicker of the pre-digital memory, football in the time of maverick authenticity, an age of mud, of landlines, of not wearing a seat belt, of smoking in pubs, of the casually discarded woodland porn mag, of Barry Davies shouting: “Oh, it’s magnificent and can’t they just taste it” while mods throw darts at each other in the background, because old fun is the best fun.

This is, of course, both deluded and incorrect, because football encourages such feelings and because many middle-aged men are already both of these things. But Palmer is genuinely unusual in the modern game. He turns up in strange spaces, finds gullies and currents in between those static pegs.

Right now he is perhaps the only truly creative English player out there, in the sense of inventing the game in front of him, dishing up in those moments the pure pleasure of a story being told in real time.

He even looks a little unusual in an era of hyper‑athletes. Palmer is light and mobile. He can turn with balletic grace. But he also has that gangly, mischievous physicality, like a very clever cartoon alpaca has worked out how to put on a royal blue football kit and run around occasionally doing amusing celebrations.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

From here Palmer will benefit from having a very good club manager who gets his position. At Bayer Leverkusen Xabi Alonso designed an entire team around getting the best out of Florian Wirtz, the “free electron” in the structure.

Beyond this, Palmer is clearly the player the national team should have been configured around after Euro 2024. It made some logical sense not to pick him for the World Cup, because merit and fitness are also important. But Thomas Tuchel simply has to play Palmer, Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane together now, even if you have to pack the team with cement sacks and tins of beans to make it work, because this is just incredibly hot, and there is literally no other point in playing these games.

But it isn’t just the football. Palmer is also just weirdly likable. There is a temptation to cast him as a Lego-haired blank, some kind of urban idiot savant, a human being made entirely from white bread, energy drinks and discarded phone cases. But he’s clearly very smart, and also very modern in his own way.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer’s persona is unbothered, wry and oddly gentle. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

This is another element of the Palmer persona. He looks unbothered, wry and oddly gentle. But the blankness is a thing, a way of being in the middle of all that glare. Palmer gives you nothing to bite on, no gaps in the armour. He even seems weirdly post-race, or just non-race, some kind of bowl-headed omni-man.

It is both an attitude and a shield of sorts. There’s a thing young people do on the internet, known as Nonchalance. This is all about projecting indifference and impassive facial expressions, appearing comically unbothered while chaotic things happen around you. In the picture with Central Cee at the Coke thing they’re both doing it, staring blankly into the camera open but also closed.

Palmer seems to do this naturally. He will sit with his legs crossed while a group of angry men have an on-pitch brawl nearby. He will have the sense of raw dramatic irony to look genuinely amused on the live TV feed as the referee stands right in the middle of the Chelsea huddle, one of the most comically weird sub-moments of the modern age.

There is a theory nonchalance is a political attitude, a response by the post-Gen-Z demographic to the challenge of making the world you find less incoherent, less intrusive on your space, a blank against the constant wall of noise, dogma and ideological boilerplate hurled your way.

Even the way Palmer plays has a kind of shrug about it, an existential creativity, making up your own patterns, making the world small, you-sized, following the lines in front of you.

One of the best bits of Monday night’s game was his interview after. Sky’s reporter Emma Saunders asked Palmer: “How ready are you for this season?” His response was: “Did you not watch the game?” – which from some old‑school, spam-faced football man might have sounded a bit weird, a bit off on power dynamic, a bit man-woman.

But it really wasn’t that at all. Palmer was already laughing. Saunders laughed back. And it was just a nice moment, banter-stuff, mate-chat, playing the game in front of you. English football has such an interesting figure here, not just a brilliant footballer, but a distinct presence, a way of existing in the middle of all that heat. Let’s try not to break him this time.

Sports.title: De Zerbi wants one more signing for Tottenham before transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi is keen to add one more signing to his Tottenham squad and has said outgoing deals are also possible before Tuesday night’s transfer deadline.

De Zerbi had dinner on Thursday night with Spurs’ owners and key executives and they discussed a final push to a window that has already exceeded his expectations. The manager welcomed Omar Marmoush to the club on Thursday from Manchester City and is preparing to involve him in Saturday’s home game against Newcastle. Spurs have also been linked with a move for Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

“I didn’t expect a market like we have done,” De Zerbi said. “I think we can do one player more and in one specific position. Yesterday we went for dinner with the owner, with Vinai [Venkatesham, the chief executive], with Johan [Lange, the sporting director] and with Enrico [Venturelli, De Zerbi’s assistant]. We spoke about this.

“It can be possible out or in. The transfer market is crazy and we have to be able to find the new players. If some players go out, leave, or to make another player [come] in … I don’t know. We are very happy with the market we have done until now. It has been more than my expectation at the beginning.”

De Zerbi is open to trimming his squad and mentioned midfielder Pape Sarr as one possible departure. “We have to see in the last day of the market what can happen with him,” he said. “I’ve been very clear with every player. If you speak clearly at the beginning you can’t expect a surprise. The players who want to leave, they left. Maybe we have some players who want to leave and they are waiting for the offer. We are waiting for the offer. To stay here, they have to feel proud and happy.

“If you want to leave and you have not found the offer, it’s your problem, not my problem. I give respect, I kiss you, I hug you, but at the end [they] have to stay calm inside the dressing room. And not to speak too much because the rules have been clear.”

De Zerbi said Mohammed Kudus, who has been out since January with a thigh injury, could return to the bench against Newcastle. He added that Micky van de Ven was “right to play” – in other words to start. He will make a decision on whether to start Pedro Porro and Sávio or use them as substitutes. “Marmoush is available to play, maybe also [at] the beginning of the game,” he said.

De Zerbi considered his established, senior options for the front line, excluding No 10s – Kudus, Sávio, Marmoush, Dominic Solanke, Richarlison, Mathys Tel and Wilson Odobert.

“Odobert is injured for a long time [after ACL surgery],” he said. “Before February, March, he is not available. And then maybe one of these players can leave before the end of the window. I think we are not too many players [in this department.]”

De Zerbi made clear he wanted to include Dejan Kulusevski in the squad he submits to the Premier League after the closure of the transfer window. The attacking midfielder last played on 11 May 2025. Spurs are putting no timeframe on his return from a knee problem.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I hope and I will be very, very happy to see Kulusevski inside of the list and I want to put Kulusevski inside because he is working very well and he’s a different player,” De Zerbi said. “Also Xavi Simons … before March, April, he’s not ready [after ACL surgery]. Kulusevski feels good, he’s improving day by day. He deserves it because he suffered too much for his age. I’m not speaking of him as a player but as a human.”

De Zerbi said he had paid for the meal with the club’s top brass at an Italian restaurant and he was effusive in his praise of how they have driven an expensive reboot of the squad. Spurs have spent £304.5m this summer – a figure that does include the £50m purchase obligation on Marmoush, which is due next summer. He has joined on an initial loan.

“Really, it’s the first time [in my career] that I didn’t push to complete the squad,” De Zerbi said. “They pushed to build [with] the top players. Johan Lange was brilliant in terms of ideas to make solutions. Also, Vinai. I remember when we closed the Sandro Tonali deal, Vinai made a video call to me when I was on holiday and he had a big smile.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa close on Jackson and Mbaye as Emery clears air with departing Watkins
Sports.content:
Unai Emery said Aston Villa were embarking on a “new chapter” as he prepared to welcome Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson and Paris Saint-Germain’s Ibrahim Mbaye in a near £100m remake of his forward line.

Jackson, for whom Villa have paid an initial £47.5m, is in line to make his debut at home to Arsenal on Monday and the club are finalising a move for Mbaye, who will also cost about £47m. They needed to reshape up front after accepting a £50m bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins and are bringing in further funds by selling Emiliano Martínez to Chelsea for £7.5m.

Jackson and Mbaye have been longstanding targets for the Villa manager. The 18-year-old winger Mbaye, a Senegal teammate of Jackson, was one of the preferred options to strengthen a key position. He played 24 Ligue 1 games for PSG last season, 10 from the start. In recent days, Villa pushed to sign Rafael Leão from Milan but the Portuguese winger is poised to join Galatasaray, whom Villa will visit in the Champions League.

Jackson was Emery’s No 1 target to replace Watkins, who declined the offer of a new contract in favour of a £50m move to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal. Both deals are yet to be formally confirmed. The one for Jackson could rise to a club-record £65m with add-ons.

Emery said Watkins’s departure reduced him to tears and he revealed the England striker apologised to him and his teammates for refusing to play in the 4-0 defeat at Brighton last weekend, leaving Villa without a recognised striker.

“I can tell you his commitment and his behaviour was fantastic always,” Emery said. “He told us after the match he was sorry and he told us that he made a mistake, that he was wrong. We accepted it, the players as well, because he always had very good behaviour and commitment with the club, with us and with me.

“For me, he is a fantastic guy, an even more fantastic a guy than a player. I told him bye with a huge hug and a small tear but now it’s a new chapter here with Nicolas Jackson. A new chapter, we replace him and of course all the best to Watkins in Saudi. With Nicolas Jackson replacing him, we are of course happy.”

Emery dismissed the idea that the manner of Watkins’s departure could tarnish his standing among supporters. Watkins is Villa’s record goalscorer in the Premier League era, with 91 goals across 221 league appearances. “The four years working with him have been a high-level relationship with him as a professional,” Emery added. “Last week I was a little bit disappointed. I was disappointed, but we spoke about it, and now clear. One mistake is not closing all the good things he did here. For the supporters as well. He is class, and I think it’s a legacy here.”

View image in fullscreen Maxim De Cuyper makes it 2-0 to Brighton on a bad day for Aston Villa. Photograph: James Marsh/Shutterstock

Emery said the £50m fees generated for Watkins, who will be 31 in December, and Konsa, who turns 29 in October, were “crazy” given their ages. “We don’t want to be a club to sell players, but the responsibility is to accept it … because for the club it is a good deal. It does not change our objectives.”

Emery acknowledged his side must perform much better against Arsenal than did against Brighton to avoid a second successive defeat. Leon Goretzka, who signed from Bayern Munich on Thursday, could make his debut against the champions, while Zion Suzuki could also feature for the first time after his £30m move from Parma, replacing Martínez.

“Maybe we are not performing like we were performing but the objective is to get to the same way we did, the same performances we had,” said the Villa manager. “We will need time. Last year we showed we needed time. On Monday we will see, [whether] we will need more time or if some players are progressing quickly.”

It promises to be a busy end to the window for Chelsea who, as well as closing in on Martínez, have explored a move for the Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara while they wait for Manchester City to submit their first official offer for Enzo Fernández.

City are yet to make contact with Chelsea over a deal for Fernández, who is desperate to leave before Tuesday night’s deadline. Chelsea are considering their next move and have Camara on a shortlist that also includes Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton. The Senegal international is not seen as a like-for-like replacement for Fernández but would strengthen Xabi Alonso’s midfield options if the Argentina international joins City.

Chelsea are aware of Bournemouth’s determination not to sell Scott and have received similar messages from Palace regarding Wharton, while Arsenal are understood to have knocked back an inquiry for Martín Zubimendi.

Although there have been suggestions that a deal for Fernández will be close to £106.7m, he will only be allowed to leave if Chelsea’s terms are met. Sources have warned City may have to pay more than the west London club’s initial £120m asking price for the 25-year-old.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Guéhi versatility crucial as Bouaddi arrives

Enzo Maresca has a shiny new £85m midfielder he could select for a debut but he may want Ayyoub Bouaddi, at 18 years old, to have a bit of time watching on from the bench to learn about the Premier League from his elders. The Moroccan may not have expected one of those to be a centre-back by trade. Marc Guéhi will be eager to make a triumphant return to Crystal Palace and may well have the opportunity to do so from central midfield, where he played last weekend in the victory over Bournemouth, scoring the equaliser. The centre-back was a surprise selection in the blocker role next to Elliot Anderson, but equipped himself admirably and was not limited to the dirty work, often being found in more advanced positions in open play and happy to have the ball at his feet. His long-term future is unlikely to be outside defence but further proof of Guéhi’s adaptability will be a positive for Maresca, as a long season awaits. Will Unwin

Crystal Palace v Manchester City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 Liverpool need to stop Gibbs-White

“It is just not personnel,” insisted Andoni Iraola in response to Liverpool conceding two goals to quick Newcastle transitions in his first Premier League game as the club’s head coach. Some long-term faults cannot be rectified overnight – although that did not prevent some hysterical reactions to the performance at St James’ Park – and, with Liverpool prioritising wingers in the final days of the transfer window, the answer to this particular weakness, as Iraola indicated, lies on the training ground. Morgan Gibbs-White revelled in the spaces behind Liverpool’s midfield last season as he – and set pieces – helped Nottingham Forest to a second successive league win at Anfield. Iraola does not want to curb Ryan Gravenberch’s attacking instincts but greater tactical discipline and willingness to do the dirty work from the entire Liverpool midfield will be needed to stop Gibbs-White producing a repeat performance. Forest’s new record signing, Liam Delap, has also been registered in time to play. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Everton note Cherries’ set-piece struggles

There were so many encouraging takeaways for Bournemouth despite an agonising late defeat at Manchester City. The catalyst for City’s turnaround was Marc Guéhi’s 84th-minute equaliser, the England defender heading in unmarked at a corner, after wasting a near-identical earlier chance. For Bournemouth, it was a familiar source of pain; only Liverpool conceded more set-piece goals in the top flight last season (20), with the Cherries and Crystal Palace both conceding 18. Bournemouth sought to address their vulnerability in the summer by hiring their first dedicated set-piece coach in Nicolas Gagnon, who worked with Canada at the World Cup and previously at Southampton and in Saudi Arabia. Only Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United and Aston Villa claimed more points away from home than Everton last season and David Moyes’s centre-backs, Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski, will be licking their lips if Bournemouth do not sharpen up their act. Ben Fisher

Bournemouth v Everton, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Bournemouth were again undone by a set-piece goal as they lost 2-1 at Manchester City. Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images

4 Too early for a relegation six-pointer?

Contrasting opening weekends for Coventry and Hull, harsh reality dealt out against the dream scenario lived out. At Arsenal, Coventry were well beaten by the champions, while in East Yorkshire, Manchester United were soundly, deservedly, defeated. Despite contrasting starts, both teams remain warm favourites for relegation. Two defeats in a row for Frank Lampard’s team would dim the optimism of a summer of expectation. Hull seek to extend the reverie of last week though Coventry are unlikely to be caught as cold as United last week, and surely cannot defend set pieces so badly. The last three Championship matches between these two teams ended in draws, last season’s meetings goalless, although both squads have since been upgraded by brisk transfer business. At Hull, much is expected of Lucas Herrington, who missed Australia’s fateful penalty against Egypt at the World Cup. The teenage defender shone against Stoke in the Tigers’ successful midweek Carabao Cup assignment. John Brewin

Coventry v Hull, Saturday 3pm

5 Tottenham keen for Tonali to tick

It has not taken long for Sandro Tonali to be reunited with his former teammates. After succumbing 3-0 on the opening weekend at Brentford, a home victory will be the minimum requirement for Tottenham. Roberto De Zerbi and his players will be desperate to show that things have changed after a busy summer in the transfer market. Tonali will be a key part of that; he was the only central midfielder who made it past half-time in west London, so at least has minutes in his legs to build on. The Italian will be eager not to suffer at the hands of a team that served him well after bringing him to England. Tonali is supposed to make his new team tick and a rousing home debut would do a lot for everyone’s confidence, while defeat would bring plenty more questions. WU

Tottenham v Newcastle, Saturday 5.30pm

View image in fullscreen Sandro Tonali (left) faces his old club Newcastle after a difficult debut against Brentford. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

6 Acheampong fights to stay with Blues

This is an important moment in Josh Acheampong’s development. The 20-year-old academy graduate did not have many opportunities last year but he started in Xabi Alonso’s back three when Chelsea beat Fulham on Monday. It was a big vote of confidence from Alonso in the young defender, who played well, and may indicate that Acheampong will stay at Stamford Bridge this season. Several clubs are interested in the England youth international and there is talk of a loan before the transfer window shuts, but Acheampong would strengthen his position further if he is selected again for Sunday’s home game against Brighton. Jacob Steinberg

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea v Brighton, Sunday 2pm

7

On Monday night, Jamie Carragher told a Sky Sports audience that he thought Sunderland might be relegated this season. The former Liverpool defender compared Régis Le Bris’s team to the Sheffield United side managed by Chris Wilder that went down in 2020-2021 – their second season after promotion – and suggested Sunderland were “arrogant”. How will Le Bris’s players respond against Fulham at the Stadium of Light on Sunday? Has the moment arrived to end a winless Premier League run against the west London club stretching back 12 years? If there are legitimate concerns about the ability of Le Bris’s players to cope with a Europa League campaign, regular Sunderland watchers struggle to buy into the accusations of arrogance, let alone the analogy with a very different Sheffield United side. Nonetheless, last Saturday’s 2-1 defeat at Ipswich has prompted a certain anxiety, leaving Wearsiders hoping Nordi Mukiele is fit enough to raise defensive standards. Louise Taylor

Sunderland v Fulham, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Sunderland fans have bristled at Jamie Carragher’s prediction for their team’s season. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

8 Leeds look to strengthen as Bees buzz

Subplots abound at Elland Road as Leeds and Brentford meet after two wins apiece from their first competitive matches of the season. There is the goalkeeping beauty contest between Daniel Farke’s showpiece summer signing, James Trafford – who has two clean sheets in his opening games – and Brentford’s Caoimhín Kelleher. Further forward, fans can ponder the question of which centre-forward, the Leeds favourite Dominic Calvert-Lewin or his opposite number, Igor Thiago, will prove the more incisive. Similarly, the technical area tactical duel involving Daniel Farke and Keith Andrews looks extremely hard to call. Away from the pitch, Farke is hoping to win a race with Sunderland to sign Marseille winger Igor Paixão for about £30m as the Leeds manager urges his board to strengthen. “I’m happy with my group and my signings so far,” said Farke. “But we know we can definitely improve our squad. That is what Leeds supporters and Leeds United deserve.” LT

Leeds v Brentford, Sunday 2pm

9 Carrick under pressure to deliver

Manchester United are bloody-nosed and Ipswich definitely delighted after the tale of each team’s results on the opening weekend. At Hull, Michael Carrick’s team played with zero cohesion and conviction and went down to a miserable 2-0 loss. At Portman Road, Gary O’Neil’s side hosted Sunderland and claimed a rousing late 2-1 win, so arrive at Old Trafford with a bounce in the step. Carrick has to lift his men and get a result – preferably victory. A loss, at home, to another promoted team, would begin the latest inquiry into a United manager: a predicament suffered by all of Sir Alex Ferguson’s successors. Jamie Jackson

Manchester United v Ipswich, Sunday 4.30pm

10 Villa fans bid farewell to Konsa

At a time when the manner of a player’s departure feels particularly pertinent, especially at Aston Villa, Ezri Konsa can expect a warm reception on his return. Konsa could make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against his former club, where he excelled across seven seasons. A £12m buy from Brentford in 2019, Konsa surely represents one of their finest signings in the Premier League era. He joined fresh from a single season in the Championship with Brentford and left as an England regular and a Europa League winner. Konsa’s role in Villa’s recent success should not be overlooked. Unai Emery can be judged by Villa’s extraordinary run of league finishes – seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth – but also his track record of turning promising talents, such as Konsa, into fully fledged internationals. BF

Sports.title: Champions League draw: Arsenal face Real Madrid, Man City get Barcelona and PSG
Sports.content:
Arsenal face mouthwatering assignments against Real Madrid and Bayern Munich as they bid to go one better than last season’s agonising near miss and win a first Champions League title.

Mikel Arteta’s side were pipped on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in the final three months ago and will be expected to cruise through this season’s league phase. The bulk of their draw appears kind but they are tasked with a visit to the Allianz Arena to play Bayern, whom they beat 3-1 at the Emirates Stadium last November, and host Real, who are once again under the charge of José Mourinho. Two seasons ago, Arsenal beat the Spanish giants 3-0 at home in a quarter-final first leg, Declan Rice scoring two memorable free-kicks.

Arsenal will also welcome Borussia Dortmund, Lille and the Azerbaijani debutants Sabah to north London. Their other away fixtures involve trips to Napoli, Slavia Prague and a reunion with their ex-player Héctor Bellerin at Real Betis.

Manchester City will swiftly renew acquaintances with Rodri when they visit Barcelona during Enzo Maresca’s first Champions League campaign in charge. They will greet Kevin De Bruyne and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium, just as they did last season in cruising to a 2-0 win. Their other home ties bring an enticing meeting with the reigning champions, PSG, a tie against Sporting and a visit by AEK Athens. Trips to Porto, RB Leipzig and Lens will round off their schedule.

The return of Manchester United to Europe’s elite competition throws up home games with Bayern, Roma, RB Leipzig and Sabah. Michael Carrick’s team will travel to Como, who are managed by Cesc Fàbregas, along with Atlético Madrid, Sporting and Villarreal.

Liverpool will host Atlético, Porto, Villarreal and Lens. They visit Lask, the newcomers who sensationally beat Celtic on Tuesday, along with Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Inter in a relatively kind-looking set of games.

Aston Villa, ravaged in recent weeks by the departures of key players, will hope to have strengthened sufficiently for a home tie with PSG and a visit to Barcelona. They will be heartened by a stirring performance in their recent Super Cup defeat to Luis Enrique’s side in Salzburg. Borussia Dortmund, Fenerbahce and the Norwegian new boys Viking Stavanger will also visit Villa Park. Unai Emery will also take his team to Club Brugge, Galatasaray and Slavia Prague.

Quick Guide Premier League teams' UCL opponents Show Manchester City: PSG (home), Barcelona (away), Sporting (h), Porto (a), Napoli (h), Leipzig (a), AEK Athens (h), Lens (a). Liverpool: Atlético Madrid (h), Inter (a), Porto (h), Club Brugge (a), Villarreal (h), Fenerbahce (a), Lens (h), Lask (a). Arsenal: Real Madrid (h), Bayern Munich (a), Borussia Dortmund (h), Real Betis (a), Lille (h), Napoli (a), Sabah (h), Slavia Prague (a). Aston Villa: PSG (h), Barcelona (a), Dortmund (h), Club Brugge (a), Fenerbahce (h), Galatasaray (a), Viking (h), Slavia Prague (a). Manchester United: Bayern (h), Atletico (a), Roma (h), Sporting (a), Leipzig (h), Villarreal (a), Sabah (h), Como (a). Order of fixtures to be confirmed by Uefa Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

While Chelsea did not qualify for European competition this season, their home will still host Champions League football. The Ukrainian champions, Shakhtar Donetsk, still unable to play continental matches in their homeland, will stage home games there. Real Madrid are the most high-profile of their four visitors, meaning Mourinho will return to his old stomping ground.

PSG’s bid to win a third successive Champions League title involves home league games against Barcelona, Roma, Galatasaray and Slovan Bratislava, as well as trips to Villarreal, Como, City and Villa.

The first set of fixtures will be played on 8 and 9 September. The schedule and dates for all eight match weeks will be announced on Saturday.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic weigh-in descends into chaos as British star PUSHES rival off stage - before being SLAPPED
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic had to be pulled apart by security after their heavyweight weigh-in descended into chaos when Hrgovic was pushed off the stage before slapping his British rival.

The two heavyweights exchanged heated words during their face-off before lining up for one final set of photographs.

But when Hrgovic stepped in front of Itauma, the Brit shoved him forward, sending his opponent tumbling off the stage.

A furious Hrgovic immediately climbed back up and slapped Itauma, who then went berserk as both men attempted to fight before security rushed in to drag them apart.

The extraordinary scenes came just 24 hours before Itauma's first shot at becoming heavyweight world champion.

It was a notable change from the 21-year-old, who has remained largely calm throughout the build-up despite Hrgovic's repeated attempts to get under his skin.

Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic had to be pulled apart by security after their heavyweight weigh-in descended into chaos

Itauma started the chaos when he pushed Hrgovic off stage before his rival slapped him

Itauma had previously dismissed his rival's insults as 'schoolground banter', while Hrgovic has tried to provoke him at almost every opportunity during fight week.

The British heavyweight had even told his manager not to nibble at Hrgovic during Thursday's press conference, seemingly determined not to be drawn into any of the mind games.

But after keeping his composure throughout the week, it was Itauma himself who finally snapped at the weigh-in.

And while it offered a side to the unbeaten heavyweight that few have seen before, those watching appeared to love it.

Hrgovic was still furious when he spoke after the confrontation and vowed to 'smash' Itauma when the pair meet in the ring tomorrow night.

Itauma, meanwhile, admitted that he had been unable to resist the temptation to react.

'I had a scratch to itch and I had to do that today,' he said.

Sports.title: Sky Sports forced to apologise for Rayan Cherki's x-rated interview after he called his performance 's***' - despite scoring TWICE - as Erling Haaland smirks alongside him following Man City's win at Palace
Sports.content:
Sky Sports forced to apologise for Rayan Cherki's x-rated interview after he called his performance 's***' - despite scoring TWICE - as Erling Haaland smirks alongside him following Man City's win at Palace

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rayan Cherki left fans confused and in stitches after he described his match-winning display in Man City's victory over Crystal Palace as 's***'.

Cherki starred at Selhurst Park by scoring twice in the second half, with Erling Haaland also adding a brace in the 4-1 victory.

The result means Enzo Maresca has two Premier League wins from two matches since replacing Pep Guardiola after his side overcame some testing moments in the first half against the Eagles.

Cherki was awarded the Player of the Match award but his post-match interview with Sky Sports certainly got supporters talking, with the broadcaster forced to apologise after he swore.

'My performance is so-so,' he said. 'In the first half, we didn't find the space, and I played so s***.

'When I see Enzo (Maresca) wants to change (substitute) me, I don’t like that, and I need to show them I want to play, I want to score, I want to give an assist to Erling.

Sky Sports were forced to apologise after Man City star Rayan Cherki said he 'played s***'

Cherki's comments came despite him scoring twice in City's 4-1 victory over Crystal Palace

'Because today I didn't give a lot of balls for him so next time I want to give him a lot of balls.'

Cherki's first goal saw him poke home after he demonstrated superb skill and quick feet to take the ball past several Palace defenders, before his second was a long range strike that took a slight deflection.

And when pressed for thoughts on his first strike, Cherki showed his humility and instead outlined his desire for the club to have a memorable campaign.

He added: 'I'm very happy for the win, see you next week. Pep [Guardiola] was a big story, we will start another story. We want to prove it and we are here for that.'

Enzo Maresca disagreed with Cherki's assessment of his display, although admitted he perhaps wasn't playing at his peak in the first period.

'He’s happy,' the City boss said of Cherki after the game. 'His performance was very good, not because of the two goals but how he worked off the ball.

'He has to press. He was in charge of Wharton when Palace had the ball. His game was a complete game on and off the ball.

'He loves football. So it is much more easy to work with him. Then he is Rayan. We know how good he is, the quality he has. In this moment, he is helping the team with his assists and goals and there is no doubt he will help the team in the future.

'He was probably not playing at his level in the first half but overall I was happy with his performance off the ball. In the second half, he scored twice and he is much more happy.'

Haaland, who smirked as Cherki swore on TV, joined the plaudits for the attacking midfielder and added: 'It's been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we'll be back, we just need a few games.

'We played well, it's a new manager but we've been playing together, with the addition of a few new players, for a long time.'

'We know what to do, and we just need to trust Enzo. This is the right step in the right direction for everyone.'

On Cherki's first goal, midfielder Elliot Anderson said: 'I'm just sat back watching. I see this every day since I've joined, him, Phil (Foden)... they've got so much talent. It's no surprise, to be honest. The talent they have is scary.'

City made it two Premier League wins from two games under Enzo Maresca with the victory

Meanwhile, Jamie Redknapp was similarly full of praise for Cherki following the game, with the Sky Sports pundit labelling the Frenchman a 'genius'.

'After Rayan Cherki painted a masterpiece - an incredible goal - City started to play and got a real hold on it,' he said. 'Cherki felt like the difference because his two goals came at such an important time.

'He just had such an amazing effect on the game and it was absolutely wonderful to see him. He is a genius, the things he can do with a football are absolute genius.'

City, who are still hoping to add more players before the transfer window closes on Tuesday, return to action next Saturday when they entertain Coventry City.

Sports.title: Atletico tell Julian Alvarez to join Arsenal or stay at the club, Aston Villa confirm £65m Nicolas Jackson signing and Spanish club joins race for Man United star Joshua Zirkzee: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Atletico tell Julian Alvarez to join Arsenal or stay at the club, Aston Villa confirm £65m Nicolas Jackson signing and Spanish club joins race for Man United star Joshua Zirkzee: WINDOW WATCH

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Atletico set Alvarez deadline amid Arsenal interest

Atletico Madrid have given Julian Alvarez until Sunday to make a decision over his future.

The Spanish side have told the ex-Man City star to move to Arsenal or stay at the club.

Alvarez is missed Atletico Madrid training for a third day running on Friday, but later trained alone.

Alvarez has been absent citing illness since Atletico told the Argentina striker they would not sell him to Barcelona.

Club CEO Gil Marin told Spanish media: ‘I’ve been in the football world for more than 30 years. My word is one of the few things I have. As long as I am CEO, Julián Alvarez will NOT be transferred to FC Barcelona. That is absolutely certain.’

Arsenal are willing to pay up to £128m for Alvarez if he opts to join them now.

With Atletico refusing to sell him to LaLiga rivals Barcelona, Arsenal are viewed as the only destination for Alvarez if he wants to leave Atletico.

Julian Alvarez missed training for the third day in a row as he pushed to leave Atletico Madrid

Hutchinson set for Milan switch

Nottingham Forest will listen to offers for Omari Hutchinson with AC Milan considering a loan offer for the winger.

Hutchinson became Forest’s record signing a year ago when he joined from Ipswich for nearly £40million but boss Oliver Glasner does not see the 22-year-old as a regular starter.

Milan have an interest in Hutchinson, who would be open to the move, but are unlikely to offer a permanent deal.

A loan with an obligation to buy is the likeliest offer at this stage.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Emotional Emery reveals Watkins goodbye - as Jackson is confirmed

Unai Emery revealed Ollie Watkins impending move to Al Hilal had reduced him to tears as he leapt to the defence of the under-fire forward.

Watkins infuriated Aston Villa fans when he did not appear in last weekend’s 4-0 defeat at Brighton, even though he was the club’s only fit centre-forward.

At the time, Emery did nothing to protect Watkins when asked about his absence. But on Friday he delivered a lavish tribute to the England man and said the £50m fee for the 30-year-old was too good to turn down, while confirming Nicolas Jackson would replace him.

Emery said: ‘I told him goodbye with a huge hug and a few tears. After the Brighton game he was sorry and told us he made a mistake, that he was wrong.

‘We accepted it and so did the players. He was always very committed and behaved well with us and with me. He’s a fantastic guy, even more than he is a player. Now it’s a new chapter here with Nicolas Jackson and we wish Ollie all the best in Saudi Arabia.

Reunited. This time in claret & blue.



Aston Villa is delighted to announce the signing of Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea 🇸🇳 pic.twitter.com/s2P8j6uKJa — Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) August 28, 2026

‘Ollie had fantastic years here always scoring and playing even when he was injured. Last week I was a little disappointed but we spoke about it. One mistake does not cancel all the good things he did here for the supporters.

‘It’s crazy that for a 30-year-old we can have £50m.’

Nicolas Jackson has joined for £65m from Chelsea having taking his formative steps in the professional game under Emery at Villarreal.

Emi Martinez was also on the brink of sealing a move to Chelsea – the fourth transfer deal between these clubs in less than six weeks.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Atletico monitoring Zirkzee

Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee is on Atletico Madrid’s radar as they anticipate a late bid from Arsenal for Julian Alvarez.

Zirkzee has an offer from Fiorentina, while Juventus and Napoli are interested and some Premier League clubs are also weighing up late offers.

SIMON JONES

City and Spurs battle for Gakpo

Manchester City continue to rival Tottenham for Liverpool winger Cody Gakpo.

Liverpool have maintained they must have two more forward players in place before they contemplate selling the Netherlands international and even then it would have to be a substantial fee.

Liverpool have yet to receive an official approach from either club.

City are also pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. Despite links with Liverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister as a back-up option, no contact has been made.

City are also pursuing parallel negotiations for Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye who has three years on contract and would cost around £80million.

SIMON JONES

Liverpool have yet to receive an official approach from any club for Cody Gakpo despite links

Ward-Prowse is a Saint... again!

Southampton have confirmed the signing of James Ward-Prowse from West Ham for a fee understood to be £800,000.

Ward-Prowse rejoins the Saints on a two-year deal, having previously made 410 appearances for the club.

Ward-Prowse joined West Ham in a £30m deal in 2023, and also spent time on loan at Nottingham Forest. However, he fell out of favour with boss Nuno Espirito Santo.

'It feels a bit surreal. The last couple of days have been pretty intense, but I’m delighted to be back, and to be wearing the red and white again is truly special,' Ward-Prowse said.

SIMON JONES

Lights, Camara, action for Chelsea as they brace for Enzo bid

Chelsea are weighing up a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara as they anticipate Manchester City's bid for Enzo Fernandez.

Chelsea are considering bringing in two midfielders with City expected to pay over £120m for Fernandez.

Talks were held between the clubs yesterday, as reported by Daily Mail Sport, over Camara who also attracted a £40m offer from Crystal Palace this summer and various enquiries.

Monaco are interested in Tottenham's Pape Matar Sarr on loan but face competition from Nottingham Forest.

SIMON JONES

Spurs join race for Ndiaye

Tottenham have joined Manchester City by showing interest in Iliman Ndiaye of Everton.

Both Spurs and City are in for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo also, should the Anfield club agree to sell.

Ndiaye has three years left on contract and is valued around £80m.

Spurs want to add more quality to their new-look attack before the deadline.

Gakpo has been their priority but City's presence means they will need alternative options also.

SIMON JONES

Tottenham Hotspur are showing an interest in Everton's star man Illiman Ndiaye

Collyer collared by Baggies

West Brom have agreed a £3million deal for Manchester United midfielder Toby Collyer.

The total package is potentially worth up to £7.6m for the 22-year-old.

United have also inserted a 40 per cent sell-on clause for any future sale.

SIMON JONES

Overy travelling to Sydney

Manchester United youngster James Overy will fly to Australia tonight as he closes in on a permanent switch to Sydney FC.

The 18-year-old, who moved to United’s academy set-up in 2024, has featured across Under-18s and Under-21s but did not break through to the first team.

Daily Mail Sport understands that he is in line to get a three-year deal with Sydney FC, who are not paying a fee. Overy will complete his move following a medical on Monday.

EXCLUSIVE BY NATHAN SALT

Valencia interested in Liverpool's Elliott

Liverpool winger Harvey Elliott is being targeted by Spanish side Valencia.

The 23-year-old has interest from a number of clubs with Lazio and Napoli among them but Valencia are hopeful they can tempt the England U21 international to link up with coach Carlos Corberan, the former West Brom boss.

Liverpool have still to receive an official approach but are aware of the interest.

Elliott had a tough time at Aston Villa last season where he was on loan with an obligation to buy at £35m following 10 games.

Clubs are exploring another loan.

SIMON JONES

Valencia are on of a number of clubs interested in Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott

Bolton confirm signing of Bazunu

Bolton have confirmed the signing of goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu from Southampton. Bazunu has signed a three-year deal at the club.

The 24-year-old said: 'It's a club with massive history. I see it as a place where I can come and progress my personal career, while helping the team with their ambitions of getting back to where they belong.'

SIMON JONES

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi holds transfer summit with Tottenham owners after £400m spend - as Spurs boss reveals aims for final days of the window
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi holds transfer summit with Tottenham owners after £400m spend - as Spurs boss reveals aims for final days of the window

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi is planning to include Dejan Kulusevski in his Premier League squad as the Tottenham winger closes in on a return to full fitness.

Kulusevski, 26, has been out for more than 15 months after suffering a serious knee injury in May 2025.

His recovery has been littered with complications and setbacks and the disappointment of missing the World Cup, but the Swede finally seems to be making steady progress.

'I hope and I will be very happy to see Kulusevski inside [the squad],' said De Zerbi. 'I want to put Kulusevski in the list because he is working very well, very hard. He's a good guy and he's a different player.

'If he feels good like now, he's improving day by day, it's great watching him. He deserves it because he has suffered too much for his career for his age. I'm not speaking of him as a player but as a human. He deserves to be inside the list.'

Kulusevski's inclusion in the 25-man list to be confirmed after Tuesday's transfer deadline would restrict De Zerbi in other areas with a limit of 17 overseas senior players.

Roberto De Zerbi revealed he is set to include Dejan Kulusevski in his Premier League squad

De Zerbi also shed light on a transfer summit he held with the club's hierarchy earlier this week

Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons, also recovering from serious knee injuries, are unlikely to be named in the squad.

'Odobert is injured for a long time,' said De Zerbi. 'Before February, March, he is not available. Xavi Simons before March, April, he's not ready.'

Spurs have signed eight players this summer and are still searching for a left winger before the deadline, with Cody Gakpo of Liverpool a top target.

Pape Matar Sarr is most likely to leave as things stand although, after completing the signing of Omar Marmoush, Spurs would entertain interest in Richarlison, who has one year remaining on his contract plus a one-year option.

Meanwhile, De Zerbi picked up the bill as Tottenham's powerbrokers met for dinner to plot their final moves of the summer transfer market.

The Spurs boss and his assistant Enrico Venturelli were joined by members of the ruling Lewis family, chief executive Vinai Venkatesham and sporting director Johan Lange at an Italian restaurant in London on Thursday.

They have invested close to £400million in new players since flirting with relegation last season and will not rule out more business, with Cody Gakpo of Liverpool a top target as they try to reinforce on the left wing.

'I think we can do one player more and in one specific position,' said De Zerbi, ahead of the first home game of the Premier League season against Newcastle. 'We went for dinner and we are all on the same page. There is a very good connection.

'I am not pushing. It's the first time I didn't push to complete the squad. I didn't push. They pushed to build it with the top players. It's not my business the transfer market. I didn't expect one transfer window like we have done.'

Spurs have signed eight new players and recouped almost £150m with sales, a figure which can increase with bonus add-ons.

It is the first summer transfer window since Daniel Levy was ousted as chairman. Transfer activity was led by Lange, Venkatesham and director of football operations Rafi Moersen. Nick Beucher, son-in-law of Vivienne Lewis, has become increasingly influential since the power shift, almost a year ago.

They have twice broken the club's transfer record to sign Mateus Fernandes from West Ham for £85m and Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100m.

'Johan was brilliant in terms of ideas to make solutions,' said De Zerbi. 'Vinai, when we closed the Tonali deal, made a video call to me when I was on holiday and he had a big smile, very happy.

'We went for dinner before the Chelsea game last season with Vinai and Johan, and it's a part of our job to organise and make the last plans in the last days of the transfer market, to speak about the condition of the players and the transfers we can do in the next three or four days. There is seriously a great relationship with all of them.'

Sports.title: Rayan Cherki gets the Enzo Maresca era up and running as Man City thump Crystal Palace - but here's why Pep Guardiola's successor still has much work to do, writes JAMES SHARPE
Sports.content:
Rayan Cherki gets the Enzo Maresca era up and running as Man City thump Crystal Palace - but here's why Pep Guardiola's successor still has much work to do, writes JAMES SHARPE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Who needs control when you have Rayan Cherki? Why does it matter who Enzo Maresca plays in midfield, or how he’ll replace Rodri, when he’s got the magical feet of this majestic Frenchman to win him games of football?

When Manchester City trailed with four minutes to go at Bournemouth in Maresca’s first Premier League match in charge, he set up the equaliser and then the winner. At Selhurst Park, as this new chaotic City look like it might wobble again, he scored twice to put all worries to bed.

His first was simply sublime. Collecting Phil Foden’s pass, he jinked his way through a tight crowd of four Palace defenders to poke the ball beyond Dean Henderson. Then, just three minutes after a Gianluigi Donnarumma own goal had made life nervy again, he blasted a second past him from 25 yards. Game over.

When Erling Haaland added a second of his own five minutes from time, it certainly was. There is still much to do but the Maresca era is up and running.

The task of inheriting a great club from a great manager is never a straightforward task, especially when the very kingdom itself is in need of a structural rebuild.

Just ask David Moyes or Unai Emery. Even a Premier League title didn’t keep Arne Slot around for long.

Man City thumped Crystal Palace 4-1 after an impressive display at Selhurst Park on Friday

Rayan Cherki dazzled again as he scored a brace to pick up the Player of the Match award

It means Enzo Maresca has two league wins from two since replacing Pep Guardiola

So, the early days of Maresca’s reign in the post-Pep Guardiola era always threatened to be jittery, even more so when the rock on which it was built in Rodri was no longer there.

City were blown away by Arsenal in the Community Shield, albeit in a glorified friendly. They trailed at home to Bournemouth for most of the game. Maresca doesn’t know his best team yet. In an early flash of his maverick predecessor, willing to fling unexpected players into unexpected positions, Maresca started centre-back Marc Guehi in midfield against Bournemouth, but returned him to defence at Selhurst Park against his former club.

For all that relentless, endless control that defined the Pep glory days, the Maresca one often just screams chaos. Palace, in the opening minutes of their first Premier League home game under Pierre Sage, had this unbalanced, uncertain City side backpedaling. Eddie Nketiah bombed past Ruben Dias down the Palace left and forced a fine low save from Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Daichi Kamada cut inside down the same side and fired in a shot that Abdukodir Khusanov had to head over his own crossbar. As Anan Khalaili geed up the crowd after another Palace opening, it felt like City might falter again.

The hope is that City’s new £86m signing Ayyoub Bouaddi, the maths student, chess player and national debating champion, will help restore that sense of control. He came on for his debut late on when the game was won. City still want Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, too, to add further physicality to a midfield that Maresca is currently trying to mix and match.

Without it, this is a City side currently relying on moments of quality instead of periods of dominance. And why not, when you have a front four that can provide it in a flash. That’s just what they did to take the lead after 17 minutes.

Antoine Semenyo was given far too long to pick his spot, curling his cross towards Haaland who outjumped Palace defender Chris Richards and sent a towering, looping header over a sprawling Dean Henderson to open his account for the season.

At least that put to bed any concerns that shaving off his flowing blond locks might have left him, like Samson, bereft of his powers. Still, when you’ve scored in every Premier League game you have played against Palace, who are we to doubt him.

Haaland, like his compatriot Jorgen Strand Larsen for Palace, sported a black armband in memory of Norway’s King Harald, who died on Friday aged 89.

Erling Haaland earlier gave City the lead when his looping header beat Dean Henderson

Haaland added the gloss on the victory with a second goal late on as City cruised to victory

Palace made it 2-1 briefly when Yeremy Pino's free kick deflected in off Gianluigi Donnarumma

There was even a chance for a debut for City's new midfield man Ayyoub Bouaddi

Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City: MATCH FACTS Palace (3-4-2-1): Henderson 5; Canvot 5.5, Richards 6, Tomiyasu 5.5 (Disasi 74, 6); Khalaili 7 (Mingueza 75), Kamada 6.5, Wharton 7, Mitchell 6; Nketiah 6 (McNeil 68, 5.5), Pino 7 (Gozo 69, 5.5); Stand Larsen 6 (Guessand 63, 5.5) Scorers: Donnarumma OG 56 Booked: Khalaili Manager: Pierre Sage 5 Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 5.5; Khusanov 7 (Reis 89), Dias 7, Guehi 7.5, Gvardiol 7 (Kovacic 75); O’Reilly 7 (Braithwaite 89), Anderson 7.5 (Bouaddi 82); Foden 8, CHERKI 9.5 (McAidoo 82), Semenyo 7.5; Haaland 9 Scorers: Haaland 17 + 84, Cherki 54 + 59 Booked: Cherki, Anderson Manager: Enzo Maresca 8 Referee: Andrew Madley 7.5

Phil Foden should have doubled City’s lead a few minutes later but, somehow, blazed over the bar from inside the box with no Palace player in sight. Foden couldn’t believe it, and neither could Maresca, who turned away and clasped both cheeks with his palms.

At times, City turned on the style. Nico O’Reilly, the newest partner for Elliot Anderson in midfield, nutmegged Kamada following a remarkable turn in the middle of the pitch before firing wide.

At many others, though, they showed why they will need to find some semblance of control if they are to flourish under Maresca.

Palace had so many openings but lacked the final touch. Tyrick Mitchell headed wide from a superb Adam Wharton cross. Chris Richards sent another free header from a free-kick weakly into the hands of Donnarumma. At the start of the second half, Mitchell fizzed a ball across goal but Nketiah couldn’t get a strong enough contact.

The hosts briefly made City wobble in between Cherki’s two stunners when World Cup winner Yeremy Pino’s beauty of a free-kick beat Donnarumma, struck the crossbar and rebounded in off the goalkeeper’s back.

City, though, won’t find all their opponents so generous in their wastefulness as Palace and certainly not when they have to take on Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad or make the trip to the Nou Camp.

Still, when you’ve got someone as magical as Cherki to decide matches, you can’t help but wonder whether any of that really matters.

Sports.title: Rangers and Celtic hit with stadium closures and heavy fines as SFA get tough following Ibrox shame game
Sports.content:
Rangers and Celtic hit with stadium closures and heavy fines as SFA get tough following Ibrox shame game

The Scottish Football Association have ordered Rangers and Celtic to play their next Scottish Cup home ties behind closed doors as a punishment for the shameful violence which marred the Old Firm derby back in March.

Both clubs will also be forced to pay £100,000 to their opponents over the loss of ticket revenue after the SFA issued hefty sanctions and full stadium closures.

A section of Celtic supporters spilled on to the pitch to celebrate after their team had won the cup tie via a penalty shootout last season.

Rangers fans then ran on to retaliate, with flares and missiles being thrown, as well as police officers and stewards being assaulted. A ten-year-old child was also struck by a coin.

It was the first time a full allocation of just over 8,000 tickets had been made available to away fans, something which Rangers flagged up to the authorities amid obvious pre-match concerns.

In total, 37 arrests have been made thus far and the disorder led to an independent review being commissioned by the SFA.

Fans of both Rangers and Celtic stormed the pitch in a chaotic Scottish Cup tie at Ibrox

The report, led by Mark Blackbourne, found that ‘life-threatening violence’ had been possible, and that a more serious catastrophe had only been narrowly avoided.

Blackbourne’s report was also critical of the football authorities for the lack of meaningful punishment dished out to clubs in the past over fan disorder.

But the SFA bucked that trend yesterday by taking the unprecedented move of ordering both Old Firm clubs to play their next Scottish Cup home fixtures behind closed doors.

It effectively represents a form of strict liability, something which Scottish clubs have consistently rejected in the past.

Celtic were the first to have their say – and they claimed they had been left ‘shocked’ by a ‘disproportionate’ punishment.

An official club statement read: ‘We are shocked by this disproportionate punishment for a relatively small incursion by Celtic supporters at a moment of emotion and celebration.

‘Our club has never defended supporters entering the field of play and we have repeatedly taken action when it occurs. However, we understand the part emotion plays in football and would have expected the context and distinction in behaviours to have been taken into account by the panel.

‘Another important distinction is that, on this occasion, Celtic were not the home club, responsible for stadium safety arrangements.

‘We will study the panel’s report and reasoning when it is available and will thereafter consider our next steps.’

Rangers responded later, acknowledging their sanction and revealing visiting Celtic fans would be granted only 300 tickets for the upcoming Premier Sports Cup tie at Ibrox.

An injured steward is dragged to safety amid the mayhem that unfolded at Ibrox

An Ibrox statement read: ‘Rangers can confirm that the away allocation for the forthcoming Premier Sports Cup fixture at Ibrox against Celtic will be 300 tickets.

‘Since the clubs last considered away allocations, the Blackbourne Report has been published and our sanction issued. Together with the events of March 8 and our assessment of the current risk, these developments have informed our planning for this fixture. Matchday safety remains our top priority.

‘Since March 8, there have also been further pitch invasions involving Celtic supporters. The Blackbourne Report demonstrated how quickly an initial incursion can escalate into wider disorder involving both sets of supporters. Preventing another pitch incursion is therefore an important part of reducing the risk of further disorder at this fixture.

‘Following the recent cup draw, Rangers approached Celtic with proposals aimed at finding a sustainable way forward. Celtic responded eight days later, and that response did not address our concerns around accountability and deterrence.

‘Rangers has not seen the clear acknowledgement, condemnation or deterrent messaging we believe should follow events of that seriousness from Celtic.

‘We are willing to work constructively with all stakeholders and authorities involved in matchday safety for these fixtures. However, the risks currently identified will only be reduced through greater accountability, effective deterrence and constructive joint working.

‘We have previously raised concerns where risks identified by the club were not, in our view, given sufficient weight, including in relation to the increased away allocation for the 8 March fixture. Rangers will not be deterred from taking decisions it believes are necessary to protect our club, our stadium and our fans.

‘Finally, we note the decision of the Scottish FA Tribunal published today and will now consider the outcome in full, including its implications, before determining any further steps.’

Sports.title: Coco Gauff hits back at 'absurd' US Open requests from friends and family... as mom issues 'blunt' warning to people scrounging off tennis star
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff has lifted the lid on the 'absurd' ticket requests she receives ahead of the US Open - a day after her mother warned family and friends not to bother trying to get in their box at Flushing Meadows.

Gauff will be one of the headline attractions when tennis fans descend on New York for the final Grand Slam of 2026. The 22-year-old won her maiden major title at the 2023 US Open and she will be among the favorites to lift the trophy this year.

But ahead of the tournament, which kicks off on Sunday, Candi Gauff issued a 'blunt' warning to loved ones and hangers on that the world No 4 is already out of guest tickets.

'Dear Family and friends,' she wrote on Instagram. 'I apologize in advance for this blunt, but necessary statement. I know you are very excited about Coco playing in the US Open. Me too!!! Coco's guest ticket request have already been accounted for.

'Unfortunately, I will not be able to hook you up with a ticket. Please make arrangements to purchase a ticket. Side note, never ask for more than 2 tickets.

'Coco is grown now and she has her own friends that she is honoring tickets for the match. Thank you for your continued support.'

Coco Gauff has lifted the lid on the 'absurd' ticket requests she receives ahead of the US Open

Her mother warned family and friends not to bother trying to get in their box in New York

'Coco's guest ticket request have already been accounted for,' Candi Gauff wrote on Instagram

The message went down well with some of Gauff's compatriots. 'Honestly we all need a @candigauff in our life,' Danielle Collins wrote. Madison Keys, meanwhile, commented: 'Iconic'

On Friday, Gauff was asked about her mother's comments, with the American admitting she 'did not know she was posting that.' But the world No 4 echoed her sentiments and opened up on the 'absurd' requests that are made.

'It was needed. It was directed toward a few family and friends,' Gauff explained. 'To be honest people come out the woodworks - you haven't spoken to someone for years, they don't say congrats or happy birthday or nothing and then they're like: "Oh, I'm in New York. Can I have 8 tickets to your match in your box please?"

'They give us tickets here but you know, they were selling in advance. So it's not like I can give all these people tickets. Last year they were really stressed out between my mom and my dad trying to accommodate everyone.

'If we have it, we'll give it. It was just stressful for them. A lot of people personally don't have my number. They don't reach out to me. They'll reach out to them or someone on my team.

'I don't know who the person who sent her a text this year where she felt that was the final straw... but somebody must've sent her something and she was like, I need to make a post.

'Specifically in New York it's just crazy. New York and Wimbledon are the ones I think people wanna come to. We try our best to accommodate everyone. But some of their requests are.. you'd be surprised how absurd they are.'

Those friends and family who missed out on Gauff's guest tickets face paying eye-watering prices to have a chance to see the 22-year-old.

A grounds pass for the opening day of the tournament is currently on sale for $314, while the cheapest seat at Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first night session costs $172.

Sports.title: Premier League footballers living in Cheshire's exclusive 'Golden Triangle' forced to knock hundreds of thousands off asking price of their mansions
Sports.content:
Premier League footballers living in Cheshire's exclusive 'Golden Triangle' forced to knock hundreds of thousands off asking price of their mansions

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Premier League footballers are knocking hundreds of thousands of pounds off the asking prices of their homes in a bid to sell them.

The stars in Cheshire's so-called 'Golden Triangle' and its surrounding areas are having to slash the cost of their mansions to secure sales.

Many are former footballers for the likes of Manchester United and Manchester City - but even current big names are being dragged into the struggle.

Manchester City and England man Phil Foden chopped £825,00 off the asking price for his home in Prestbury - plunging it from £3.25m to £2.4m.

A sale at that price meant that the 26-year-old, who lives with his childhood sweetheart Rebecca Cooke and their three children, lost £450,000 on the price he paid for the pad.

Now a spate of other former and current Premier League names find themselves in a similar predicament.

Premier League players are being forced to slash the prices of their homes in Cheshire's 'Golden Triangle' to sell them (pictured: Phil Foden's house, which he lost £450,000 on)
