Sports.title: No changes as FIA completes second ADUO power unit development analysis | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA has confirmed the results of its second analysis of Formula 1 engine performance under its Additional Development Upgrade Opportunity regulations.

The sport’s governing body has decided not to allow any further development opportunities beyond those announced following its first analysis. The first analysis followed the Canadian Grand Prix and the second concluded following the Hungarian Grand Prix at the beginning of the summer break.

Under the first analysis, all power unit manufacturers except Red Bull-Ford were given extra opportunities to introduce upgrades.

“The FIA has undertaken thorough and exhaustive analysis as part of our ADUO review process,” said Nikolas Tombazis, the director of the FIA’s single-seater division. “With the release of the findings of period two, we are confident that, based on the quality of the data, its analysis is incredibly robust, giving us a high level of confidence in our findings.

“We also have to respect the confidentiality and intellectual property of the teams and their Power Unit Manufacturers in disseminating any details from the findings.

“This is the first year of ADUO so naturally there are areas which we may evolve over time, in discussion with all the PU manufacturers.”

The third ADUO period will cover last weekend’s Dutch Grand Prix up to the Mexican Grand Prix in November.

Sports.title: Stats: McLaren win Formula 1’s last Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort – again | 2026 Dutch Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
The Dutch Grand Prix became a Max Verstappen stronghold when it returned to the calendar six years ago. The Red Bull driver won each of the first three grands prix at his home track.

However the final three editions of the race were all won by McLaren. Lando Norris claimed back-to-back wins either side of the summer break.

This was the last Dutch Grand Prix for the foreseeable future as Zandvoort does not have a deal for F1 to return. Just as when it hosted the last race of its previous stint as an F1 venue in 1985, McLaren won the final race.

On that occasion Niki Lauda claimed his 25th and, as it turned out, final victory. He had announced his retirement plans at his home event one week earlier.

Norris’s win was his 13th, giving him as many as two-times world champion Alberto Ascari and David Coulthard. He also took his 18th pole position, giving him as many as Mario Andretti, Kimi Raikkonen and Rene Arnoux.

Although Ferrari failed to win on the modern Zandvoort layout, they remain the most successful team at the track with eight wins to McLaren’s six. Ferrari’s last win came courtesy of Arnoux in 1983. Mercedes also did not manage to win at Zandvoort during its return; their only victory at the track remains Juan Manuel Fangio’s 1955 triumph.

Charles Leclerc denied Norris a hat-trick by recording the 13th fastest lap of his career. He now has as many as 1980 world champion Alan Jones, plus Jacky Ickx and Riccardo Patrese.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Regardless of how the weekend turned out, Andrea Kimi Antonelli was always going to go to his home race next week as the world championship leader. With a 59-point lead, he is now guaranteed to head the standings when F1 departs Europe for the final nine ‘flyaway’ rounds.

George Russell claimed his fourth sprint race victory but failed to make any inroads on Antonelli’s points lead after following his team mate home in the grand prix.

Liam Lawson made his 50th appearance at a grand prix weekend back at the team he made his 15th and 16th participations with at the beginning of last year. His second stint at Red Bull was much more successful than his first as he finished seventh, despite a 10-second time penalty.

His return to Red Bull came about due to Isack Hadjar’s unfortunate injury. This also prevented Hadjar extending his run of seven consecutive points-scoring finishes.

Verstappen’s first-lap retirement meant Lawson was the only driver to score points for Red Bull. Prior to that Verstappen had never failed to finish outside the top two places at Zandvoort.

He has now gone 12 rounds without a grand prix victory. This is the second-longest win-less streak of his career, only behind the 30-race spell between his first and second grand prix victories in 2016 and 2017.

Yuki Tsunoda returned and finished one place outside of the points. Had he reached 10th he would have tied Kamui Kobayashi as Japan’s all-time top points-scorer.

The second half of 2026 ha begun much more brightly for Aston Martin following their upgrades in the last two races. Fernando Alonso took ninth place, their best result of the season so far. Team mate Lance Stroll remains one of only three drivers yet to score this year, along with the Cadillac duo, but he must fancy his chances now.

Sports.title: Domenicali hopeful Verstappen’s new deal will end talk of F1 exit | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Stefano Domenicali hopes Max Verstappen’s new Red Bull contract will put an end to claims he could leave Formula 1.

The Red Bull driver, who is one of the strongest critics of F1’s current regulations, said his uncertainty over agreeing a new deal with his team had been “mainly about actually continuing in Formula 1.”

Speaking ahead of Sunday’s Dutch Grand Prix, Domenicali said “the news of Max staying in Red Bull for the next couple of years is a cherry on the cake for this weekend.”

“It’s great news, [I’m] very proud and happy because Max is a world champion, world class person that has a great personality in the sport and I cannot see [imagine] Formula 1 without him.”

In May, Verstappen said it was “mentally not doable for me to stay” if F1 did not alter the power balance between the combustion and electrical parts of its engines next year. It subsequently announced changes will be introduced over the next two years.

“The rules are slowly getting a bit better and, let’s say, I’m willing to live with it,” said Verstappen. “Hopefully by 2030 it opens up another opportunity, potentially with V8 engines coming in, to look again.”

Domenicali hopes Verstappen’s new deal will quieten speculation the popular four-times champion will leave F1. “[I’m] very happy that this news now is official and all these talks that have been happening so far will be out of place,” he said. “Now I’m sure that the focus [will be] for the team to be as good as possible to give Max the best car that he can.”

Doubt continues to hang over the status of F1’s final two rounds this season, which will be held in the Middle East. The conflict in the region has already led F1 to abandon its plans to race in Saudi Arabia in Bahrain this year and arranged for the latter event to take place in Malaysia instead.

Domenicali indicated no decision has yet been taken to cancel the final two rounds in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. “The calendar, as I said, is confirmed, so there are still a few tickets to be sold in Abu Dhabi,” he said. “Everything is progressing well, and we stay focused on delivering the calendar we promised at the beginning of the year.”

Sports.title: Who’s who in the Tszyu Zoo
Sports.content:
In 2020, Tszyu had the first key fight of his career, facing fellow Australian and former world champion, Jeff Horn. Tszyu battered the former champion using his jab, uppercuts and big right hands to the body and head, hurting him and breaking him down to force a retirement TKO in the eighth round.

Tszyu’s next key fight was against the durable and courageous Japanese fighter, Takeshi Inoue, in November 2021.

This was Tszyu’s 20th fight of his career, and this fight proved to be a turning point for him as a fighter on the international stage. Although he was outgunned, Inoue fought with passion and pride to give Tszyu a hard fight and take Tszyu the twelve-round distance for the first time.

In March, 2024, Tszyu, on late notice, traveled to Las Vegas to face the towering junior middleweight champion, Sebastian Fundora, in what was an iconic fight for both boxers. Both fighters, splattered in blood and both hurt by accident and intention, gave the fans a fight to remember, with Fundora winning by a split decision. Inexperience and a stubborn refusal to accept defeat cost him the fight.

Another key fight was his fight against the Chechen come-forward fighter, Bakhram Murtazaliev in October 2024, just six months after recovering and healing from a bad cut to the top of his head in the Fundora fight.

Tszyu was battered into a state of shock and disbelief, then knocked down numerous times until the fight was stopped in the third round in Orlando, Florida.

Tszyu returned to Sydney and back to the drawing board . Six months later, he took a confidence-building fight against the unrated and limited fighter Joey Spencer, to then go back three months later to face Sebastian Fundora for the WBC light middleweight championship of the world.

In the return match, Fundora fought smart, outboxing Tszyu by using his skill , timing, and natural ability, beating the Australian to force a corner retirement at the end of the 7th round.

Tszyu came back in December, beating unknown Anthony Velasquez in Sydney.

After beating Denis Nurja in April 2026, Tszyu focused on the Spence Jnr fight, and the win was deemed by many as a tremendous victory. My view on this is yes, it was good to have the name of Errol Spence Jnr on his record, but the key factor in the decision win was that it has kept his career alive.

So where does he go from here? With a new management and coaching team around him, as well as fighting at his new weight of 160 pounds, what’s next?

Erislandy Lara is the WBA middleweight champion. With a good record of 32 wins ( 19 KOs), 3 losses, and 1 draw, the Cuban southpaw is 43 years old, and since 2022, he has battered Gary ‘Spike’ O’Sullivan, destroyed Michael Zerafa, proved to be too much for Danny Garcia, and in December 2025, he beat Johan Gonzales on points. Lara has not fought in 2026. On any given night, a motivated Lara is and can be an awkward and dangerous opponent for anyone.

Carlos Adames is the WBC middleweight champion. The Dominican Republic puncher has a great record with 25 ( 18 KOs) and 1 defeat. He is 32 years old, and he consistently fights only once a year.

Aaron McKenna is the IBF middleweight champion. The newly crowned Irishman is 27 years old, and he is an unbeaten, well-schooled boxer . His record stands at 21-0. ( 10 KOs) McKenna is 6’3, and he has a 75-inch reach. He won the World title, beating the Italian Etinosa Oliha in early August, and prior to that he outboxed the experienced Liam Smith. He has a tremendous work rate, and he has speed.

Denzel Bentley. WBO middleweight champion. With a record of 22 wins ( 18 KOs), 3 losses, and 1 draw, the 31-year-old Englishman was the interim champion, to then be elevated to the WBO champion due to Janibek Alimkhanuly relinquishing his title to move up to super middleweight.

My view is, all roads lead to Jermell Charlo. He could be the path of least resistance for a big money fight. He is still a name, and he was the junior middleweight champion of the world. He has been inactive since being outboxed and outmuscled by Saul Canelo Alvarez in September 2023. He has a record of 35-2-1 with 19 KOs. He would be moving up in weight to meet Tszyu, and that would suit the 36-year-old at this stage of his career. If staged in Australia, the fight will sell as there has been some history of trash talking by both fighters, and for Tszyu, this could be his swan song, so it makes great business sense for him and also lucrative for Charlo.

The question is, will Tszyu wait and fight for a mandatory shot at one of the world champions, or will he make a move on Charlo?

Gary Todd is an international best-selling author, and he has been involved in all aspects of the sport of boxing for decades . Check out his latest book, “ Greatest Ever Boxing Champions. Their mindset. Their Workouts, Their Journeys.”

Sports.title: Boxing’s Strangest Records Need More Than Numbers
Sports.content:
Willie Pep recorded 229 victories, Archie Moore won 186 times and Sugar Ray Robinson collected 174 wins. Fritzie Zivic, Henry Armstrong, Nicolino Locche, Kid Gavilan, Julio Cesar Chavez and Roberto Duran also passed 100.

Their totals came from a boxing economy built around regular ticket sales at local halls and arenas. Boxers needed another booking to collect another purse. Staying active also kept them in fighting condition, reducing the need for the long rebuilding camps associated with current appearances.

Modern headliners receive broadcast guarantees and purses that allow them to earn more from one event than an earlier fighter might have made across dozens of appearances. The financial pressure to box every few weeks has disappeared at the highest level.

A Loss Once Meant Something Different

Promoters today market a perfect record as proof of superiority. One defeat can reduce a fighter’s television value, weaken his negotiating position and send his handlers searching for several favorable opponents to rebuild him.

Earlier generations had less reason to protect every number. A defeat could be treated as experience because another fight might be available within weeks. Weekly club shows also gave developing professionals room to accumulate 40 or 50 contests before reaching the national level.

That regional structure has largely disappeared. Many prospects now move from long amateur careers into televised professional fights without passing through the same volume of club competition.

The Fighters Paid to Test Prospects

Kristian Laight finished with 12 wins, 279 losses and nine draws, but calling him one of boxing’s greatest losers misses his value. He completed 300 fights and was stopped only five times. That required defensive awareness, composure and a clear understanding of how to survive difficult rounds.

Promoters trusted Laight to test developing fighters without turning every bout into a reckless war. He provided rounds, exposed mistakes and helped matchmakers judge if a prospect was ready to advance.

Reggie Strickland served a similar role during a 360-fight career, compiling 66 wins, 276 losses and 18 draws. Peter Buckley recorded 32 wins, 256 losses and 12 draws while facing future champions including Naseem Hamed, Kell Brook, Acelino Freitas and Gavin Rees.

Both men regularly traveled into the territory of promoted fighters. Winning a close points decision under those conditions was difficult, especially when the local boxer represented the financial investment behind the event. Their records cannot be separated from the purpose they served.

Too many upsets would cost a journeyman future calls. Getting knocked out too easily offered little developmental value. The job required operating between those extremes.

Boxing records tell us who won and lost, but not what each fighter was being paid to accomplish. Wickwar’s 340 victories preserve the remains of an industry built on constant competition. Laight’s 279 defeats expose the workforce that allowed another generation to learn its trade.

Both records belong in boxing history, though not for the same reason.

Sports.title: Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson Faces Shawn McCalman For WBA Intercontinental Title
Sports.content:
Coming out of the renowned Upton Boxing Center, Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson started his pro career with thirteen consecutive victories. Back in August 2023, Simpson took a costly trip to Atlanta, as he suffered his first defeat by way of majority decision to Vladimir Hernandez.

Ten months later, Simpson made a return trip to Atlanta for another Overtime Boxing event, and he lost via controversial split-decision to Raiko Santana. Truck Simpson bounced back with a first-round stoppage victory over Trevon Smith.

In his next outing, Simpson suffered another setback, as he was outpointed by Jahi Tucker. Once again, Simpson took a moment to regroup, and then he bounced back with a second-round TKO victory over George Sosa.

Now Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson is ready to step into the ring in front of his hometown fans to face a dangerous opponent. His adversary for this event is the Colorado native Shawn McCalman.

Similar to Truck Simpson, Shawn McCalman started his pro career with fifteen consecutive victories. He came up short in two of his last four fights, as he lost to highly ranked Diego Pacheco and the undefeated Moreno Fendero.

Now Shawn McCalman has vowed to travel to Baltimore and bring the WBA Intercontinental strap back to Colorado. This match will be a challenging bout for both fighters.

The southpaw Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson is a boxer who has all the tools. His confidence is at an all-time high, and he believes all he has to do is stay focused, and his time to shine will be right here, right now.

Simpson knows the night of September 19th will be a true test. According to a recent post, challenging nights are now a personal requirement for Truck.

Sports.title: Former Heavyweight Champion Hasim Rahman Set To Return To The Ring At Age 53
Sports.content:
Hasim Rahman has publicly stated he’s on a quest to become the oldest world heavyweight champion in boxing history. After a 12-year hiatus, Rahman will start his new boxing journey on the night of September 24th.

A native of Baltimore, Maryland, Hasim Rahman made his pro boxing debut back in December 1994 when he stopped Gregory Herrington in the first round. He would go on to win his next 28 fights.

In December 1998, Hasim Rahman suffered his first career defeat when he lost to David Tua via 10th-round TKO. Rahman would bounce back by returning to the ring and posting two consecutive knockout victories.

Rahman was starting to rebuild the momentum, but then he lost to Oleg Maskaev. Once again Rahman would regroup and then go on a three-fight win streak.

On the night of April 22, 2001, Hasim Rahman stepped inside the ring as he looked to capitalize on a golden opportunity. Standing in the opposite corner was the reigning unified heavyweight world champion Lennox Lewis.

With 39 seconds remaining in the fifth round, Rahman landed a hard right hand that sent Lewis down to the canvas. Lewis was counted out, and Hasim Rahman became the new WBC and IBF unified world heavyweight champion.

Seven months later, Lewis avenged the defeat by stopping Rahman in the fourth round. After losing the rematch, fight fans were curious about whether Hasim Rahman would fall into the category of a one-hit wonder.

Rahman would proceed to silence the doubters by going on a four-year grind. In August 2005, Hasim Rahman became a two-time world champion when he outpointed Monte Barrett and won the vacant WBC strap.

Hasim Rahman had a Hall of Fame boxing career that concluded in 2014. Now the hard-hitting former two-time world heavyweight champion is ready to return to the squared circle in pursuit of boxing history.

Back in March 1977, George Foreman retired from boxing. Foreman made his return to the sport in 1987. Seven years into his comeback, Foreman stopped Michael Moorer in the 10th round and became world champion at the age of 45.

On September 24th, the Trojan Fight League presents Hasim Rahman vs Phillip Triantafillo. Going into the fight, the question is: will Rahman start a historic comeback, or will Triantafillo play the role of the spoiler and put an immediate halt to Rahman’s return to the ring?

Sports.title: Two Minute Rounds Favor Mikaela Mayer Against Chantelle Cameron
Sports.content:
The ESPN+ main card begins at 2:00 p.m. ET and 11:00 a.m. PT. Sky Sports will televise the card in the United Kingdom beginning at 7:00 p.m. BST. Main event ring walks are projected between 9:30 and 10:00 p.m. BST.

Friday’s weigh-in ended with Mayer at exactly 148 pounds and Cameron at 147.6.

Round duration became one of the main negotiating issues. Cameron wanted 12 three-minute rounds after defeating Michaela Kotaskova under the longer format in April. Mayer held firm on 10 two-minute rounds because her WBC title could not be defended under Cameron’s preferred rules.

Accepting the shorter format allowed Cameron to get the fight made. She has since questioned her earlier belief that three-minute rounds would make stoppages easier to produce.

“Over two minutes, it’s just, ‘Bam,’ and I don’t really take a step back.”

In an interview with The Ring, Cameron explained that she had to manage her energy more carefully during the Kotaskova fight. Two-minute sessions let her attack at full pace without taking the brief rests she needed over three.

That alters the original tactical reading. Shorter rounds give Mayer an opportunity to score quickly and leave before Cameron settles inside, but they also permit Cameron to maintain pressure without conserving energy. Each one may become a race to establish command during the first 30 seconds.

Three super welterweight belts are involved, yet neither fighter was asked to approach the 154-pound limit. The contracted ceiling keeps Mayer near the welterweight division, where she has said she intends to pursue Lauren Price.

Her career has taken her from super featherweight through junior middleweight, and she considers herself a natural welterweight. Cameron spent most of her championship run at light welterweight before moving higher. Describing both as natural 154-pounders would be misleading.

Fighting at 148 reduces any physical edge Cameron might have gained by filling out further. It also means neither woman should be carrying enough additional mass to cause a major decline in punch output during the later rounds.

Cameron Must Force Mayer Toward The Ropes

Straight one-two combinations followed by a pivot away from the center line are central to Mayer’s work. Her height helps her see openings over shorter opponents, although Cameron owns the longer listed reach at 69 inches to Mayer’s 66½.

Simply following Mayer would cost Cameron rounds. She must use her jab to close exits, move her feet across the ring and make the American retreat toward the ropes.

Once there, Cameron can place her head against Mayer’s chest and shorten her hooks underneath the elbows. Her physical pressure becomes more useful in that position than the listed measurements.

Trapped opponents do not always get a clinch from Mayer. Against Maiva Hamadouche and Sandy Ryan, she often answered with volume from close range. Her willingness to trade makes her dangerous, but it also gives Cameron the contest she wants.

In her first meeting with Katie Taylor, Cameron denied her comfortable breaks and extended the inside exchanges. Remaining stationary after landing the first combination would leave Mayer vulnerable to the same approach.

A disputed split decision against Natasha Jonas already went against Mayer in Britain. Her other professional defeat, against Alycia Baumgardner, also came by split decision in the United Kingdom.

Those results may encourage her to produce rounds that are easier to score. Straight punches to the head are more visible from ringside than short hooks landing around the elbows. Cameron may perform the harder physical work without receiving equal credit if Mayer’s jab and right hand remain the cleaner shots.

The compressed rounds magnify that issue. A quick Mayer combination can create the visual impression of command before Cameron begins working inside. Her body punching must be obvious, and she cannot allow Mayer to finish with unanswered shots.

The weigh-in confrontation supplied the hostility, but Saturday’s scoring may come down to which fighter claims the first and final exchanges. Clean combinations and timely exits are essential for Mayer. Cameron has to close the ring early enough to turn each round into a sustained fight.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Shoves Hrgovic Off Weigh In Stage
Sports.content:
Itauma started it by pushing Hrgovic off the edge of an elevated stage, where a bad landing carried more danger than anything likely to happen during a standard staredown. He was upset about Hrgovic stepping in front of him, partially for a double-biceps pose. It was pretty harmless stuff, but Itauma got heated enough to shove Hrgovic while his back was turned.

Hrgovic Exposes Itauma’s Temper

Hrgovic repeatedly labeled Itauma a protected “golden child” steered carefully toward this title opportunity. The way that Itauma lost his temper today was a signal that Hrgovic’s comments have gotten to him.

The reaction exposes genuine vulnerability. Confident fighters shrug off verbal insults, flash a grin, and settle business inside the ropes. Instead, the 21-year-old met a standard pose with physical aggression, proving his patience snaps the moment he feels slighted.

Hrgovic now holds a clear psychological target. If he roughs up Itauma on the inside, leans hard during clinches, and turns early rounds into a grueling dogfight, the young puncher must avoid unraveling into reckless mistakes.

Itauma hit the scale at 241.7 pounds, while Hrgovic came in trim at 236.2. The scale numbers do not dictate tactics outright, but the Croatian’s lean conditioning favors an active plan built on movement, straight right hands through the southpaw guard, and non-stop pressure.

Itauma has not faced incoming fire from anyone carrying Hrgovic’s rare blend of size, physical power, and battle-tested experience. The opposition fed to the young prospect so far sits firmly in the journeyman category, save for a 38-year-old, faded Dillian Whyte.

Hrgovic has already faced monstrous punchers, absorbing full-force bombs from Zhilei Zhang and trading heavy artillery with Daniel Dubois. Shoving someone off an elevated stage is simple. Keeping composure once Hrgovic connects with clean right hands will prove whether Itauma is truly ready for the elite level.

Sports.title: Sugar Ray Robinson Meets His Match in Carmen Basilio
Sports.content:
The champion also held a five-inch height advantage, standing 5 feet 11 inches to Basilio’s 5 feet 6½ inches. That difference favored him at long range but helped Basilio once he got inside. His lower position allowed him to crowd beneath Robinson’s shoulders and leave little room for the sweeping left hook that had knocked out Fullmer.

Using his height, reach and faster hands, Robinson moved around Basilio, stabbed him with the jab and fired combinations before trying to regain space. Basilio followed without wasting energy on a fast pursuit. He narrowed the ring, hooked to the body and waited for Robinson to stop moving.

By the second round, their tactical contest had already become a fight. Basilio bored inside while Robinson answered with short hooks before backing away. They continued punching after the bell in the third, an early indication that neither man intended to concede physical ground.

A cut opened over Basilio’s left eye in the fifth. Robinson repeatedly found it with his jab, but Basilio treated every clean punch as an entrance fee. Once through the champion’s reach, he attacked the ribs and made Robinson work before he could escape.

Accuracy and movement gave Robinson much of the first six rounds. Those exchanges were costing Basilio, but they had not driven him from his plan. His body punching was an investment in the later rounds. Each hook to the ribs reduced the spring in Robinson’s legs and made the next attempt to create room more expensive.

Brief pauses between combinations normally allowed Robinson to reset his feet and select the next attack. Basilio removed them by following through the jab and immediately renewing the fight. Robinson could finish an assault, but he rarely had time to settle afterward.

Basilio Turns Pressure Into Control

The balance changed in the seventh when Basilio drove a left hook into Robinson’s jaw, followed with a right to the body and another shot upstairs. He had reached his preferred range. Robinson could still land the sharper punches, but he was no longer deciding where the exchanges took place.

Inside, Robinson’s height became less useful. His arms were forced into shorter arcs, reducing the leverage on his hooks. Basilio had room to dig compact punches into the ribs while keeping his head beneath the most dangerous lines of fire.

The eighth, ninth and tenth increasingly belonged to Basilio. During the ninth, Robinson found himself on the ropes as punches came from both hands. He looked tired, and each attempt to restore the jab led to another collision at close range.

Round 11 became the center of the fight. Robinson found another supply of energy and snapped jabs into Basilio’s damaged eye before opening up with combinations. Basilio absorbed the attack, forced him to the ropes and answered with a sustained assault of his own. Robinson covered, clinched and then fired back. Neither man gained command for long enough to rest.

The 12th brought another Robinson rally. His jab, straight right and left hook worsened the damage around Basilio’s eye and opened his nose. Still moving forward, Basilio returned to the body whenever the combinations ended.

During much of the 13th, Basilio looked stronger as he doubled his hooks from the body to the head. Robinson then produced one of his largest punches of the night, a late left hook that shook Basilio and nearly dropped him.

A hard right to the body folded Basilio in the 14th, but Robinson lacked the energy to sustain the attack. His best punches still carried greater speed and precision. Basilio’s advantage was that he required less recovery before starting again.

For the 15th, Robinson tried to box behind his jab and clinch whenever Basilio reached him. His mouth was open, and his movement no longer created enough separation.

Walking through the jab, Basilio drove a right into the body and followed with punches to the head. Robinson launched one final charge, but Basilio met him and continued throwing until the bell. They touched gloves after completing 15 rounds without a knockdown.

Referee Al Berl favored Robinson nine rounds to six. Judges Bill Recht and Artie Aidala gave Basilio the split decision, with Recht scoring it 8-6-1 and Aidala 9-5-1. A poll of 47 ringside writers leaned toward Basilio, 26 to 17, with four scoring it even. The Associated Press had the fight level at 6-6-3.

The scoring divided observers because the officials were judging two different forms of command. Robinson landed with greater precision and produced the larger individual moments. Basilio determined the range, sustained the pace, and made Robinson fight on his terms. Two officials valued that offensive initiative more heavily.

Under the rules then used by the New York State Athletic Commission, Basilio could not retain championships in two divisions. Winning the middleweight crown automatically ended his welterweight reign when the decision was announced.

Six months later, Robinson reclaimed the middleweight title by split decision at Chicago Stadium, winning it for a record fifth time. Basilio fought much of that rematch with his left eye swollen shut.

The Ring selected each meeting as its Fight of the Year. The first belonged to Basilio’s pressure, the second to Robinson’s adjustment, and neither man escaped without giving up part of himself.

Sports.title: WBO Russia Ban Threatens Bivol-Smith Title Fight
Sports.content:
“Now we need to work on getting the WBO to lift its sanctions against Russia, and then we’ll be able to officially announce that the fight will take place on December 12 in Yekaterinburg,” Titov said, as reported by Darshan Desai.

The agreement resolves negotiations between the promotional companies, but the championship issue remains open. The WBO has declined to sanction title fights in Russia during the war in Ukraine, applying that position when Bivol defended against Michael Eifert at the same venue on May 30.

Bivol’s WBA and IBF belts were at stake against Eifert, while the WBO allowed him to retain its title without defending it. Repeating that arrangement against Smith presents a greater difficulty because Smith is the WBO interim champion and mandatory challenger. His entitlement to face Bivol comes directly from the organization whose belt cannot presently be contested in Russia.

Smith therefore has more at risk than an ordinary visiting challenger. A fight in Yekaterinburg places him in Bivol’s home market, and removing the WBO title from the promotion takes away the main prize he spent years positioning himself to pursue. Smith has traveled for major fights against Canelo Alvarez and Artur Beterbiev, but accepting another away assignment makes far less sense if his title opportunity is reduced to a defense of Bivol’s other belts.

An exception creates a different difficulty for the WBO. The organization withheld its title from Bivol’s May fight in Russia, so reversing course seven months later requires an explanation. The greater commercial value of the Smith fight makes the change look selective unless the broader policy is being removed.

Bivol is already a unified champion rather than undisputed because David Benavidez holds the WBC belt. If the WBO refuses approval and the fight proceeds in Russia, Bivol’s three-belt collection begins separating further. Smith can contest the WBA and IBF titles, but the WBO still must decide what happens to its champion, interim champion and outstanding obligation.

Moving the event to the United Kingdom, Saudi Arabia or another neutral location preserves all three title stakes. RCC’s preference for a Bivol homecoming makes that the secondary option, but the promoters may need it if the WBO maintains the restriction it enforced in May.

December 12 may be the working date, and both sides have agreed to the fight, but Yekaterinburg has not been approved. The WBO now controls the part of the deal that RCC and Matchroom cannot settle between themselves.

Dmitrii Bivol And Callum Smith Agree WBO Title Fight

Dmitrii Bivol and Callum Smith have agreed to a date and venue for their WBO light heavyweight title fight, removing the need for the purse bid scheduled by the sanctioning body.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri confirmed that RCC Boxing, representing Bivol, and Matchroom Boxing, representing mandatory challenger Smith, had completed negotiations.

“Please be advised that the WBO World Championship Committee has received written confirmation from RCC Boxing, on behalf of WBO Light Heavyweight Champion Dmitrii Bivol, and Matchroom Boxing, on behalf of Mandatory Challenger Callum Smith, confirming that the parties have reached terms, including an agreed date and venue for the WBO Light Heavyweight Mandatory Championship Contest.

“The WBO respectfully defers to the parties to formally announce the date, venue, and event details in due course,” said Olivieri on X.

Smith, 36, is finally getting the title opportunity he has waited for, but the financial value remains unknown. Bivol’s two fights with Artur Beterbiev were backed by Turki Alalshikh and carried undisputed championship status. A mandatory defense does not have the same commercial weight.

The venue will reveal more. Saudi involvement may turn the event into another major payday. If RCC Boxing and Matchroom are financing it without that support, Smith may receive considerably less than Bivol and Beterbiev earned from their two meetings.

Inactivity presents another concern for the challenger. He has not competed since going through a 12-round war with Joshua Buatsi in February 2025 and has boxed only twice since suffering a seventh-round knockout against Beterbiev in January 2024.

Bivol, 35, underwent back surgery after his questionable majority decision over Beterbiev in February 2025. He returned in May 2026 and defeated IBF mandatory Michael Eifert by a wide unanimous decision before undergoing surgery on his injured left elbow in July.

The champion has therefore boxed only once since the Beterbiev rematch and must now return from a second operation. Smith has been inactive longer, but neither man enters under ideal conditions. Bivol must show that his elbow permits him to throw combinations freely, while his challenger must overcome approximately 18 months outside the ring.

Those two Beterbiev bouts supplied Smith with a blueprint for troubling Bivol. Sustained aggression denied him room to settle, made him expend energy, and reduced the time available for his accurate combinations.

During the opening six rounds of their rematch, Beterbiev looked capable of breaking Bivol. His work rate dropped from the seventh through the 11th, however. Once he increased the pace in round 12, Bivol again looked vulnerable and close to being stopped.

Smith cannot afford similar quiet stretches. He must cut off the ring, attack the body and maintain the pace instead of following Bivol while absorbing straight punches. Knowing the plan and executing it for an entire championship bout are very different tasks.

At six feet three inches with a 78-inch reach, Smith owns major physical advantages but has not always used them effectively. He often retreats in straight lines before settling behind a static high guard near the ropes. That habit would give Bivol the stationary target he wants for his quick multi-punch combinations.

A counter left hook remains Smith’s best chance of changing the contest with one punch. Landing it cleanly will be difficult because Bivol maintains a disciplined defensive position while jabbing and rarely leaves his chin exposed for the shot that Smith used to stop Gilbert Castillo and Mathieu Bauderlique.

High guards also give Bivol opportunities rather than discouraging him. He can split the gloves with straight punches, attack around them with hooks and leave the pocket before the counter arrives. Canelo Alvarez and Gilberto Ramirez struggled to interrupt that rhythm once he began controlling the distance.

Their common opponents underline the size of Smith’s task. Bivol neutralized Canelo over 12 rounds and divided two close decisions with Beterbiev. Smith suffered a one-sided decision against Canelo before Beterbiev dropped him twice and stopped him in the seventh. Those results do not decide this contest, but they show that the champion has handled the elite opposition that overwhelmed his mandatory challenger.

At 36, this may be Smith’s final opportunity to win a world title in a second division. That urgency may force him to take risks, yet passive pursuit will not be enough. He needs to use his reach to push Bivol backward, work the body and prevent him from resetting without becoming trapped behind his guard.

Waiting preserved Smith’s mandatory position but took away valuable time near the end of his career. He finally has the opportunity he wanted. Now he must carry out an exhausting tactical blueprint against one of boxing’s most accurate technicians after approximately 18 months without competition.

Ghana News.title: Shatta Wale: ‘I don’t have any best-performing Mahama appointee’
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian musician Charles Nii Armah Mensah, popularly known as Shatta Wale, has expressed dissatisfaction with the performance of President John Dramani Mahama’s appointees, saying he is currently unable to identify any minister or government official whose performance stands out.

The outspoken musician made the observation in an interview with GHOne TV when asked to name his best-performing ministers or presidential appointees since the Mahama administration assumed office.

In a brief but pointed response, Shatta Wale said he had no particular appointee he could single out for praise.

“So far I don’t have any, and I can give you examples why I don’t have any,” he replied.

His comments suggest a critical assessment of the performance of the government’s appointees, despite his earlier expression on the same platform of his support for President Mahama and his political ideology.

His latest remarks, however, indicate that his support for the President does not necessarily extend to all members of the administration.

Shatta Wale’s comments come amid continuing public scrutiny of government ministers and appointees, particularly over their delivery on campaign promises, responsiveness to citizens and performance in their respective sectors.

“Gov’t owes me GH¢5m” — Shatta Wale fumes over “total disrespect”

During the same interview, Shatta Wale alleged that the government owes him about GH¢5 million for promotional activities and s he undertook in support of the Black Stars’ participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

“With the World Cup that we did, you know we had to promote whatever…We were supposed to be paid. Up till now, I have not been paid. For the postings and ads, a lot. I think now they owe me about GH₵5 million," he said.

The claim has not been independently verified, and the Ministry is yet to publicly respond.

The artiste said the alleged outstanding payment had contributed to his inability to identify a best-performing minister or presidential appointee.

The artiste expressed frustration over his attempts to obtain payment, alleging that calls to officials had gone unanswered.

“Oh, not a penny. You call the minister; he will not pick. The deputy minister of finance will also not pick it. Disrespect, total disrespect in this country,” he fumed.

Ghana News.title: Shatta Wale endorses Mahama’s vision, questions appointees
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian dancehall artiste Charles Nii Armah Mensah Jnr, popularly known as Shatta Wale, has expressed support for President John Dramani Mahama’s governing ideology, while withholding a similar endorsement for members of his administration.

Speaking in an interview with GHOne TV, Shatta Wale said he was satisfied with the President’s vision but suggested that the performance of some government appointees had left him unimpressed.

“I’m happy with President Mahama [and] his ideology,” he said.

His comments come amid a broader assessment of the performance of President Mahama’s ministers and other appointees, with the musician distinguishing between his support for the President’s political direction and his reservations about those responsible for implementing it.

Shatta Wale’s position has also been placed against his own dealings with government. He recently claimed that the Ministry of Youth and Sports owed him about GH¢5 million for promotional activities he undertook in support of the Black Stars during Ghana’s 2026 World Cup campaign. The claim has not been independently verified, and the Ministry is yet to publicly respond.

The artiste said the alleged outstanding payment had contributed to his inability to identify a best-performing minister or presidential appointee.

“With the World Cup that we did, you know we had to promote whatever…We were supposed to be paid. Up till now, I have not been paid. For the postings and ads, a lot. I think now they owe me about GH₵5 million," he said.

“Oh, not a penny. You call the minister; he will not pick. The deputy minister of finance will also not pick it. Disrespect, total disrespect in this country,” he fumed.

His latest comments, therefore, present a mixed assessment of the administration, approving of the President’s ideological direction but criticising aspects of the performance and conduct of some appointees.

Shatta Wale has previously demonstrated public support for the national team and, in March 2026, pledged $100,000 towards Ghana’s World Cup campaign.

Ghana News.title: “Gov’t owes me GH¢5m” — Shatta Wale fumes over “total disrespect”
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has alleged that the government owes him about GH¢5 million for promotional activities and s he undertook in support of the Black Stars’ participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The musician said the outstanding amount covered postings, s and other promotional work undertaken as part of efforts to rally support for Ghana’s campaign at the tournament.

Speaking in an interview with GHOne TV, Shatta Wale said he was yet to receive any payment despite having completed the work.

“With the World Cup that we did, you know we had to promote whatever…We were supposed to be paid. Up till now, I have not been paid. For the postings and ads, a lot. I think now they owe me about GH₵5 million," he said.

‘Not a penny’

The artiste expressed frustration over his attempts to obtain payment, alleging that calls to officials had gone unanswered.

“Oh, not a penny. You call the minister; he will not pick. The deputy minister of finance will also not pick it. Disrespect, total disrespect in this country,” he fumed.

His comments also expose a broader concern about the relationship between government institutions and creative industry professionals engaged to support national programmes, particularly where promotional services are provided under commercial arrangements.

The claim comes against the backdrop of a broader government-led fundraising and mobilisation campaign ahead of Ghana’s participation in the 2026 World Cup.

In June 2026, the government announced the release of GH¢76 million to support the Black Stars’ World Cup campaign, including GH¢58 million for preparations and group-stage expenses and GH¢17 million to settle outstanding qualification bonuses.

Shatta Wale had also publicly supported the national team’s campaign. During a fundraising initiative in March, he and his Hotwav team reportedly contributed US$100,000 towards the Black Stars’ World Cup efforts. That contribution was separate from the payment he says is owed for his promotional work.

Ghana News.title: NSMQ 2026: Accra Academy books quarter-final spot, sends Holy Child packing after fierce battle
Ghana News.content:
Accra Academy sent Holy Child and Senya SHS packing after a tightly fought contest at the Main Auditorium, holding their nerve in the final round to retain their seeded status and book a place in the quarter-finals of the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ).

Senya SHS had a strong start, opening with a two-point lead over Accra Academy and six ahead of Holy Child.

Accra Academy stayed within reach in the second round, but the Problem of the Day brought a major shift as Holy Child answered nine questions and Accra Academy eight, while Senya SHS failed to score.

Then came Senya SHS's most difficult moment. The same contestants who had written their answers earlier wiped their work clean just seconds before time was called, believing they had spotted a mistake that needed to be corrected.

The decision left them with zero points for the round as Holy Child and Accra Academy moved ahead.

‎

‎Senya SHS recovered in Round Four, however, pulling level with Accra Academy on 36 points. Holy Child was only two points behind, leaving the three schools separated by a narrow margin going into the final round.

The Bleoo Boys pulled clear in the closing round to finish on 43 points, with Holy Child on 40 points and Senya SHS on 36 points.

The result keeps Accra Academy among the seeded schools and sends them into the quarter-finals. The Bleoo Boys have reached the quarter-finals and semi-finals on previous occasions but are still searching for their first NSMQ trophy, having last exited at the quarter-final stage after losing to Opoku Ware School.

Holy Child's return after a two-year absence ends at the One-Eighth stage, while Senya SHS, making only their second appearance at the national stage after debuting in 2025, leave with the Jupay Clean Sheet Prize.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
